title: EOL detection, normalization, and BOM stripping at buffer-construction time
referenceLocation: references/vscode/src/vs/editor/common/model/pieceTreeTextBuffer/pieceTreeTextBufferBuilder.ts:27-40 (_getEOL majority vote), :44-56 (normalize all chunks to one EOL), :99-119 (acceptChunk: BOM strip + hold back trailing \r / high surrogate so a CRLF or surrogate pair is never split across chunks), :156-186 (_finish re-attaches held char, counts a trailing lone \r); pieceTreeBase.ts:64-99 (createLineStarts counts cr/lf/crlf separately and tracks isBasicASCII in one pass), :320-353 (normalizeEOL re-chunks the whole tree at AverageBufferSize), :555-585 (getLineRawContent strips a trailing \r when _EOLNormalized is false)
mechanism:
The builder counts cr, lf and crlf occurrences while ingesting chunks. `_getEOL` picks '
' if `cr + crlf > totalEOL/2`, else '
'. If the chosen EOL disagrees with what's in the text, every chunk is rewritten with `str.replace(/
||
/g, eol)` and its lineStarts array rebuilt, so the tree is internally single-EOL. The BOM is stripped off the first chunk and stored separately on the buffer (`getBOM()`), then re-prepended only by `createSnapshot(preserveBOM)` / `getValue(eol, preserveBOM)`. `acceptChunk` refuses to end a chunk on a lone '' or a high surrogate, holding the char back so no chunk boundary ever falls inside a CRLF pair or a surrogate pair. When normalization is off, `_EOLNormalized === false` and every line read strips a trailing CR with an explicit regex. `setEOL` re-runs `normalizeEOL`, and the EOL is recorded in the undo stack (beforeEOL/afterEOL in editStack.ts:41-47) so undo restores it.
whyItMatters: Open any file written on Windows or any git checkout with `core.autocrlf=true` and our editor silently keeps a '\r' as the last character of every line. Because our view computes line ends as `nextLineStart - 1`, that CR is part of the rendered line text: the caret can be placed after it, End goes one column too far, word/subword navigation sees a spurious character, find/replace regexes with `$` misbehave, and the character is round-tripped back on save. There is also no BOM handling, so a UTF-8 BOM becomes a visible zero-width character at offset 0 of line 1 that all offsets are shifted by.

implementationSketch:
Add an ingestion step in front of `createPieceTableSnapshot` (packages/editor/src/pieceTable/snapshot.ts:43): scan the source once counting cr/lf/crlf plus isBasicASCII/containsRTL, strip a leading ﻿ into a `bom` field, pick the document EOL by majority, and if it differs, `replace(/
||
/g, eol)` before constructing buffers. Store `{ eol, bom }` on `PieceTableBuffers` (it is already a plain object spread on every edit, so this is free). Keep the internal representation LF-only — that keeps every existing '
' index in buffers.ts, virtualizedTextViewHelpers.ts and the fold/inline maps correct with zero changes — and re-expand to the document EOL only in `materializeFullText`/`readRange` when an explicit `eol` preference is passed, plus in whatever host code saves. title: Undo coalescing keyed on edit-operation type, so consecutive deletes merge and an explicit undo-stop API exists
referenceLocation: references/vscode/src/vs/editor/common/cursor/cursorTypeEditOperations.ts:942-976 (getTypingOperation / shouldPushStackElementBetween / normalizeOperationType); cursorCommon.ts:34-41 (EditOperationType: Other, DeletingLeft, DeletingRight, TypingOther, TypingFirstSpace, TypingConsecutiveSpace); cursorDeleteOperations.ts:22 and :172 (`shouldPushStackElementBefore = prevEditOperationType !== EditOperationType.DeletingLeft/Right`, forced true at :35/:184 when the selection was non-empty); editStack.ts:412-420 (_getOrCreateEditStackElement appends into the open element), :390-408 (pushStackElement/popStackElement close and reopen it); references/codemirror5/src/model/history.js:61-99 (addChangeToHistory: merge if same opId, or same `origin` where '+'-prefixed origins merge within historyEventDelay and '*'-prefixed always merge) and src/edit/options.js:155 (historyEventDelay 1250)
mechanism: Monaco keeps one *open* edit-stack element and appends every subsequent edit into it (`compressConsecutiveTextChanges`, editStack.ts:50-56) until something closes it. The cursor decides: before each operation it computes `shouldPushStackElementBetween(previousOpType, newOpType)`. The rules are (a) always stop before a non-typing operation, (b) `TypingFirstSpace` never forces a stop — so a single space glues the preceding word to the following one — while a *second* space does, and (c) otherwise stop whenever the normalized operation type changes. Deletes have their own types: consecutive Backspaces are all `DeletingLeft` so they collapse into one undo step, consecutive Deletes are all `DeletingRight`, and switching between them, or deleting a non-empty selection, forces a stop. Any command can also call `pushStackElement()` to force a boundary. CM5 reaches a similar place differently: everything inside one `operation` (same `opId`) merges unconditionally, and across operations it merges by a caller-supplied `origin` string protocol — `'+input'`/`'+delete'` merge if within `historyEventDelay` ms, `'*'`-prefixed always merge, anything else never merges. That origin string is the public extension point for undo grouping.
whyItMatters: Today every Backspace is its own undo step in our editor. Hold Backspace over a word, then press Cmd-Z: Monaco and CM5 restore the whole word in one stroke; we restore one character at a time. The same applies to Delete, to indent/outdent runs, and to any repeated programmatic edit. Our typing coalescing also has no time component, so a run typed 10 minutes apart at the same offset still merges into one undo entry. And plugins have no way to say 'these three edits are one user action' — `undoGroup` is declared in the metadata type but is never written by any caller.
ourEvidence: /Users/shaul/Desktop/D/Editor/packages/editor/src/documentSession.ts:552-565 `shouldAmendTypingRun` returns false unless `options.metadata.intent === 'insert-text'`, so backspace/delete/indent/outdent transactions (intents at :208-217) always push a fresh history entry via :544-549; :567-584 `updateTypingRun` nulls the run for any non-insert intent; :217 `readonly undoGroup?: string` — grep across packages shows the only other reference is Editor.ts:2482 reading it, never writing it; :1178-1182 `startsNewWordAfterWhitespace` is our only boundary heuristic and it puts the stop *after* whitespace rather than before it.

Backspace/delete already flow through `commitRecordedEdit`, so amending them is the same `amendEditorHistory` call already used for typing — the only new piece is a delete-aware `createAmendedTypingTransaction` that extends the recorded range leftward (for backspace) or rightward (for delete) and re-derives `inverseEdits` by concatenating the removed text. Add a public `breakUndoGroup()` on DocumentSession (we already have `breakTypingRun`) and start honouring `metadata.undoGroup` as CM5 honours `origin`: same non-empty group => always amend, different group => always break. Add a wall-clock guard (`Date.now() - runStartedAt > 1250`) to match historyEventDelay.

The undo-stop API DOES exist and the claim missed it: `breakTypingRun()` is declared on both session interfaces at /Users/shaul/Desktop/D/Editor/packages/editor/src/documentSession.ts:89 and :152, implemented at :486-488 (`this.typingRun = null`), forwarded at :898-899 and :1058, and already called around paste at /Users/shaul/Desktop/D/Editor/packages/editor/src/editor/inputSelectionController.ts:1585-1589 (`applyPasteText` brackets the edit with a break on both sides) and at documentSession.ts:681, :692, :711. The coalescing gap is real and confirmed: :552-564 `shouldAmendTypingRun` returns false unless `options.metadata.intent === 'insert-text'` (:556) and :1184-1189 `canAmendTypingTransaction` re-asserts the same; :566-583 `updateTypingRun` nulls the run for any other intent. The intent union at :206-218 lists 'backspace' and 'delete' as first-class, so both always take the fresh-entry path at :544-549. `undoGroup` at :217 is confirmed write-never: the only other reference in the repo is a read at Editor.ts:2482.

The real defect is that holding Backspace over a word produces one undo entry per character, so Cmd-Z restores one character at a time; Monaco merges the whole deletion run. The fix is small and local: generalize `shouldAmendTypingRun`/`updateTypingRun` (documentSession.ts:552-583) from a single 'insert-text' intent to a typing-run *kind* ('insert' | 'backspace' | 'delete'), amend only when kind matches and the edit is contiguous with the run (for backspace that means `edit.to === typingRun.startOffset` rather than `edit.from === endOffset`), and keep the existing `startsNewWordAfterWhitespace` boundary. Monaco's `TypingFirstSpace` nuance — a single space does not force a stop but a second one does — is worth copying since our current heuristic puts the stop after whitespace rather than before it.

title: Bounded undo history — depth cap, and serializing closed stack elements out of the live heap
referenceLocation: references/codemirror5/src/model/history.js:16 (undoDepth), :90-94 (`while (hist.done.length > hist.undoDepth) { hist.done.shift(); if (!hist.done[0].ranges) hist.done.shift() }` — pops the change *and* its paired selection entry) and src/edit/options.js:154 (`option("undoDepth", 200, ...)`); references/vscode/src/vs/editor/common/model/editStack.ts:82-140 (SingleModelEditStackData.serialize/deserialize into a flat ArrayBuffer with fixed-width selections and length-prefixed text), :200-210 (close() serializes when the element stops being appendable, open() rehydrates), :235-240 (heapSize() = byteLength + 168 overhead); vs/editor/common/services/modelService.ts:502-542 (sums element.heapSize() and drops the retained stack when it exceeds maxMemory)
mechanism: CM5 hard-caps the number of undo events at 200 and shifts the oldest off, carefully removing the selection entry that pairs with it. Monaco does not cap count but converts each undo element to a compact binary blob as soon as it stops being the append target (`close()` — which is exactly the moment the undo group ends), so the *live* representation of history is a byte buffer rather than a graph of JS objects, and `heapSize()` gives the service a real number to budget against.
whyItMatters: Our undo stack is an unbounded persistent linked list where each entry retains a whole `PieceTableSnapshot` **and** a `DocumentTransaction` containing `snapshotBefore`, `snapshotAfter`, `edits` and `inverseEdits` (the inverse edits hold the full deleted text as strings). Structural sharing makes the tree cheap, but two things are not shared: the inverse-edit strings, and — more importantly — deleted pieces are never removed from the tree. `deleteFromPieceTable` marks pieces invisible (tombstones) instead of unlinking them, so `pieceCount` only ever grows, and every retained historical root pins every tombstone that was ever created. A long editing session on a large file therefore grows monotonically in both node count (slowing every O(log n) descent) and string retention, with no eviction point anywhere. The tombstone-compaction TODO is already acknowledged in the code but has nothing to trigger it.
ourEvidence: /Users/shaul/Desktop/D/Editor/packages/editor/src/history.ts:30-53 `pushHistoryEntry`/`commitEditorHistory` push unconditionally; `size` is tracked but never compared to a limit and nothing ever truncates `undo`. /Users/shaul/Desktop/D/Editor/packages/editor/src/pieceTable/edits.ts:112-141 `deleteFromPieceTable` calls `markTreeInvisible` (tree.ts:402-418) which keeps every node. /Users/shaul/Desktop/D/Editor/packages/editor/src/pieceTable/walker.ts:8-9 comments reference an unimplemented 'tombstone-compaction TODO'. /Users/shaul/Desktop/D/Editor/packages/editor/src/documentSession.ts:220-228 DocumentTransaction retains both snapshots plus edits and inverseEdits.
implementationSketch: Add `maxUndoDepth` (default ~200) to `createEditorHistory` and truncate in `pushHistoryEntry` — since the stack is a persistent cons list, truncation means walking to the tail once and rebuilding, so instead track depth and rebuild only every N pushes, or switch `EditorHistoryStack` to a plain array with `shift()` like CM5. Truncation is also the natural trigger for tombstone compaction: once the oldest retained root is dropped, run a rebuild pass (flattenPieces filtered on `visible`, then `createTreeFromPieces` + `buildReverseIndex`) on the *current* snapshot only, and invalidate any anchors resolving to now-dropped pieces via the existing `liveness: 'deleted'` path in anchors.ts:113-135. Separately, stop retaining `snapshotBefore`/`snapshotAfter` on transactions that are already in the history stack — the stack holds them.
verifierEvidence: Confirmed absent. `grep -rn 'maxUndo|historyLimit|MAX_HISTORY|undoDepth|trimHistory|historySize|maxEntries'` across packages/*/src returns nothing. /Users/shaul/Desktop/D/Editor/packages/editor/src/history.ts:429-435 `pushHistoryEntry` conses unconditionally; `size` is computed at :434 but never read against a bound anywhere. Tombstones are permanent: /Users/shaul/Desktop/D/Editor/packages/editor/src/pieceTable/edits.ts:128 calls `markTreeInvisible`, which at /Users/shaul/Desktop/D/Editor/packages/editor/src/pieceTable/tree.ts:402-418 clones each node and flips `visible:false` while keeping every node in the tree; the acknowledged TODO is at /Users/shaul/Desktop/D/Editor/packages/editor/src/pieceTable/walker.ts:8-9. Each retained `DocumentTransaction` (documentSession.ts:220-228) holds snapshotBefore, snapshotAfter, edits, inverseEdits and both selection sets.
verifierNotes: Confirmed, but lower the priority and drop Monaco's serialization half. Monaco binary-serializes closed elements because its undo elements own full text strings; ours do not — text lives in the append-only piece buffers regardless of history, and snapshots share tree nodes structurally, so a retained entry costs a handful of objects, not a copy of the document. The genuine cost is second-order: because history pins every historical snapshot, no tombstone can ever be compacted, so the walker's O(k) boundary cost (walker.ts:8-9) grows without bound in a long editing session — a day-long session on a hot file degrades sequential reads. So the item to keep is a depth cap that lets the tail of history be dropped and thereby unblocks the tombstone-compaction TODO, not blob serialization. CM5's cap is 200 events; note it also has to evict the paired selection entry, which we would not, since our entries carry selections inline (history.ts:400-403).

title: Huge-file guards decided once at construction and permanently respected
referenceLocation: references/vscode/src/vs/editor/common/model/textModel.ts:188-191 (_MODEL_SYNC_LIMIT 50MB, LARGE_FILE_SIZE_THRESHOLD 20MB, LARGE_FILE_LINE_COUNT_THRESHOLD 300k lines, LARGE_FILE_HEAP_OPERATION_THRESHOLD 256M chars), :334-348 (the decision, with the comment '!!! Make a decision in the ctor and permanently respect this decision !!!'), :368 (_isTooLargeForSyncing), :633-643 (the three predicates), :651 (tokenization refuses), :801-803 and :871-873 (getValue / getLinesContent throw BugIndicatingError when isTooLargeForHeapOperation)
mechanism: Three independent budgets, all resolved once in the constructor from the buffer's length and line count so no later edit can flip the answer mid-session: tokenization is refused above 20MB *or* 300k lines; worker syncing is refused above 50MB; and whole-document string materialization (`getValue`, `getLinesContent`) throws above 256M characters rather than OOMing the renderer. The line-count threshold matters as much as the byte threshold — a 5MB minified bundle is one line and tokenizes fine, a 5MB log file with 400k lines does not.
whyItMatters: Nothing in our editor asks how big the document is before doing something proportional to its size. Concretely: `findController` calls `host.materializeFullText()` on every search input change, and after any edit that string is not retained, so each call walks the piece tree and joins a fresh full-size string. The diff plugin, decode plugin, merge-conflict plugin and the shiki worker client all do the same. On a 50MB file, opening find allocates 50MB per keystroke. There is also no point at which we decline to tokenize or decline to ship the document to a worker.

title: Position<->offset conversion caches: a node search cache, a last-visited-line cache, and a remainder trick that avoids the second tree descent
referenceLocation: references/vscode/src/vs/editor/common/model/pieceTreeTextBuffer/pieceTreeBase.ts:200-265 (PieceTreeSearchCache with get(offset) / get2(lineNumber) / validate(offset) which drops entries at or after an edit), :277-278 and :315-316 (instantiated with limit 1 plus a _lastVisitedLine slot), :395-416 (getOffsetAt: one descent using lf_left + getAccumulatedValue), :418-456 (getPositionAt: `out.remainder + 1` is the column directly, so a second descent via getOffsetAt only happens when the offset lands on a piece's first line), :610-630 (getLineContent memoizes the last line requested), :849-853 and :946-950 (both insert and delete reset _lastVisitedLine), :1257-1290 (nodeAt2 consults and populates the cache with nodeStartLineNumber)
mechanism: Three layers. (1) The augmented tree stores `lf_left` (line feeds in the left subtree) and `size_left`, so both directions are a single root-to-node walk. (2) `getPositionAt` gets the column for free from the in-piece remainder returned by `getIndexOf`, and only falls back to a second `getOffsetAt` descent in the boundary case where the offset sits on the piece's first line. (3) A tiny LRU (limit 1) of `{node, nodeStartOffset, nodeStartLineNumber}` short-circuits repeated lookups in the same neighbourhood — which is what actually happens during typing, multi-cursor edits, and viewport rendering — and `validate(offset)` invalidates only entries at or past the edit rather than clearing everything.
whyItMatters: Our `offsetToPoint` does two independent full descents: `countLineBreaksBeforeOffset` and then `lineStartOffset` (which is a third helper doing its own descent to find the row-th line break). `pointToOffset` does two descents (line start + line end). These run per selection per line in indent/outdent (documentSelectionEdits.ts:237-250), and per fold and per edit in foldMap/inlineMap. With 500 cursors, an indent is ~2000 tree descents, all in the same handful of pieces. There is no cache anywhere at this layer — the good `lineStarts` index we do maintain lives in the *view* (virtualization), so model-side consumers like the fold map and selection edits get none of it.

The view-level index is separate: /Users/shaul/Desktop/D/Editor/packages/editor/src/virtualization/lineStartIndex.ts.

First, make `offsetToPoint` return the column from the same descent: change `countLineBreaksBeforeOffset` to also return the offset of the last line break it passed (it already computes `countPiecePrefixLineBreaks`; have `findOffsetAfterPieceLineBreak`-style bookkeeping carry the running prefix), eliminating the `lineStartOffset` call for the common case. title: Chunked change buffer with re-chunking, and typed-array line-start indexes

title: Long-line defences: token-span splitting, render truncation with an escape hatch, and bounded coordinate magnitudes
referenceLocation: references/vscode/src/vs/editor/common/viewLayout/viewLineRenderer.ts:569-645 (splitLargeTokens, Constants.LongToken = 50, with the microsoft/vscode#6885 rationale), :471-479 (stopRenderingLineAfter truncation) and :1205 (renderOverflowingCharCount); references/vscode/src/vs/editor/contrib/longLinesHelper/browser/longLinesHelper.ts (clicking past the truncation point disables it for the session); references/vscode/src/vs/editor/common/viewLayout/linesLayout.ts:642-651 (bigNumbersDelta, quantised to a multiple of defaultLineHeight) and references/vscode/src/vs/editor/browser/viewParts/viewLines/viewLines.ts:618,674-676 (domNode height clamped to 1e6; lines positioned relative to the delta)
mechanism: Three independent defences. (1) `splitLargeTokens` caps any single `<span>` at 50 characters — splitting at spaces when ligatures or non-ASCII are involved, blindly otherwise — because browsers read character positions out of very large text nodes in super-linear time. (2) `stopRenderingLineAfter` truncates the rendered HTML at N columns and appends a rendered overflow count; `LongLinesHelper` then watches for a click at a column beyond the cutoff and flips the option off for that editor, so the truncation is invisible until the user actually needs the tail. (3) `bigNumbersDelta`: when the viewport's vertical offset exceeds 500,000px, all rendered `top` values are expressed relative to a delta that is itself floored to a multiple of the default line height (linesLayout.ts:647-648) — so the numbers browsers must lay out stay small and the sub-line phase is preserved — while the lines container's own height is clamped to 1,000,000px (viewLines.ts:618).
whyItMatters: We chose a better long-line strategy than truncation (horizontal chunk windowing), so (2) is mostly moot for us — but (1) and (3) are orthogonal to it. Our chunks can still contain very large text nodes, and our absolute row positioning uses raw document coordinates, which for a multi-million-line file exceeds the magnitudes browsers position reliably.
ourEvidence: We have the better half: packages/editor/src/virtualization/virtualizedTextViewRows.ts:1076-1115 (`shouldChunkLine` + `horizontalChunkWindow`) renders only the horizontally visible window of a long line, aligned to `longLineChunkSize` — strictly better than `stopRenderingLineAfter`. What is missing: `createRowChunk` (:1039-1075) does not cap the size of an individual text node within a chunk, and `setDirectRowText`/`isSimpleRowText` (virtualizedTextViewGeometry.ts:81-87) put an entire un-chunked line into a single Text node, so a 9,000-character line under `longLineChunkThreshold` is one enormous text node that Range measurement must scan. On magnitudes: `positionRowElement` (virtualizedTextViewRows.ts:1204-1217) writes `translateY(${top}px)` with `top = item.start`, an absolute document coordinate, and `applyTotalHeight` (:1812) sets the spacer to the full `snapshot.totalSize` with no clamp — grep for `1000000`, `maxHeight`, `33554` across src/virtualization returns nothing.
implementationSketch: For (1): in `createRowChunks` (virtualizedTextViewRows.ts:1019-1038), subdivide any text part longer than ~50-100 chars into multiple Text nodes — split at spaces when `!isSimpleRowText`, at fixed stride otherwise, exactly as splitLargeTokens does. This is invisible to `offsetToX` because `appendTextBoundaries` already iterates parts. For (3): thread a `verticalDelta` through the snapshot — computed in fixedRowVirtualizer's `scrollGeometry` as `floor(scrollTop / 500000) * 500000` re-floored to a multiple of the row height — subtract it in `positionRowElement` and add it back in the inverse mapping used by hit-testing and `selectionReveal`. Clamp the spacer height (`applyTotalHeight`) to ~1e6 while keeping the logical total in `snapshot.totalSize`, which requires the scroll position to be scaled; alternatively note this as a known ceiling and just add the `verticalDelta`, which fixes precision without the scaling complexity.
verifierEvidence: Partial is the right status, but one of the three sub-claims is FALSE and must be corrected. TRUE — we have the better truncation story: virtualizedTextViewRows.ts:1074-1113 `shouldChunkLine` + `horizontalChunkWindow` render only the horizontally visible window aligned to `longLineChunkSize`, strictly better than Monaco's `stopRenderingLineAfter` (references/vscode/src/vs/editor/common/viewLayout/viewLineRenderer.ts:471-474). TRUE — no text-node cap: `createRowChunk` (:1038-1071) puts a whole chunk's text in one Text node, and virtualizedTextViewGeometry.ts:81-87/`setDirectRowText` put an entire sub-threshold line in a single Text node, so a 9,000-char line below `longLineChunkThreshold` is one node that Range measurement must scan; Monaco caps any span at 50 chars via `splitLargeTokens` (viewLineRenderer.ts:511, 581). FALSE — 'bounded coordinate magnitudes … no clamp … grep for 1000000 returns nothing': /Users/shaul/Desktop/D/Editor/packages/editor/src/virtualization/fixedRowVirtualizer.ts:81 declares `DEFAULT_MAX_SCROLL_HEIGHT = 16_000_000` (the underscore is why the survey's grep missed it), :833-840 `nativeScrollHeightFor` clamps the DOM scroll height to it, and :843-859 `nativeScrollTopForLogical`/`logicalScrollTopForNative` proportionally remap between logical and native scroll space — Monaco's exact technique. virtualizedTextViewRows.ts:1806-1814 `applyTotalHeight` writes `snapshot.nativeScrollHeight` (the CLAMPED value), not `totalSize`, plus a compensating `translateY(nativeScrollTop - scrollTop)` on the spacer. fixedRowVirtualizer.ts:288-292 even forces immediate emit whenever the capped path is active, precisely so the spacer transform tracks every scroll delta.
verifierNotes: Status unchanged at partial, but the survey's evidence needs the correction above before anyone acts on it — we already solved the browser scroll-height ceiling, and a plan that re-implements it would be wasted work. Scope the remaining work to the text-node cap alone: split chunk text into ≤50-char Text nodes inside `createRowChunk`, and apply the same cap on the `setDirectRowText` path for sub-threshold long lines. That directly speeds up `measuredTextSegmentRect`'s Range scans and composes with claim 1's measurement fixes. The residual magnitude concern is minor and I would not chase it: `positionRowElement` (:1204-1217) still writes an unclamped logical `translateY`, so on a document past 16M logical px the transform value exceeds the clamped scroll space; float precision degrades but nothing breaks, and `logicalScrollTopForNative` keeps hit-testing consistent.

title: Grapheme-cluster movement and emoji-aware backspace (move ≠ delete granularity)
referenceLocation: references/vscode/src/vs/base/common/strings.ts:586-648 (GraphemeIterator, nextCharLength, prevCharLength), :1007-1090 (breakBetweenGraphemeBreakType, GB3-GB11), :1168-1183 (getLeftDeleteOffset), :1185-1235 (getOffsetBeforeLastEmojiComponent); references/vscode/src/vs/editor/common/cursor/cursorMoveOperations.ts:30-37 (leftPosition uses prevCharLength), :110-118 (rightPosition uses nextCharLength); references/vscode/src/vs/editor/common/cursor/cursorDeleteOperations.ts:222-231 (getPositionAfterDeleteLeft uses getLeftDeleteOffset); references/codemirror5/src/util/misc.js:143-152 (isExtendingChar/skipExtendingChars); references/codemirror5/src/input/movement.js:6-13 (moveCharLogically)
mechanism: Monaco deliberately uses two different granularities. Arrow-key movement steps a full extended grapheme cluster: `MoveOperations.leftPosition` calls `strings.prevCharLength`, which runs a `GraphemeIterator` over code points and consults a `GraphemeBreakTree` implementing UAX#29 rules GB3-GB11 (no break before Extend/ZWJ/SpacingMark, no break inside Hangul L/V/T sequences, no break inside emoji-modifier or ZWJ sequences, no break between paired regional indicators). Backspace uses a *different* function, `strings.getLeftDeleteOffset`, which first tries `getOffsetBeforeLastEmojiComponent`: it walks back over skin-tone modifiers / VS16 / keycaps, expects an emoji base, then optionally consumes a preceding ZWJ plus its emoji — so backspace on 👨‍👩‍👧 peels off one family member per press, while backspace on `e`+U+0301 removes only the combining accent. Move-left over the same text jumps the whole cluster. CM5 does a cheaper version of the same idea with a hand-written `extendingChars` regex and `skipExtendingChars`.
whyItMatters: Today an arrow key in our editor can park the caret between a base character and its combining mark, or between the two halves of a ZWJ emoji sequence. Rendering then shows the caret mid-glyph, selection highlights are half-glyph wide, and Delete/Backspace can leave orphaned combining marks or lone ZWJs in the buffer. Any user writing Hindi, Thai, Korean, Arabic, or just emoji hits this immediately.
ourEvidence: packages/editor/src/textRanges.ts:43-75 — `previousCodePointOffset`/`nextCodePointOffset` handle surrogate pairs only (charCode 0xD800-0xDFFF checks) and nothing else; `codePointSizeAt` returns 1 or 2. packages/editor/src/editor/navigationTargets.ts:206-209 `codePointOffset` is what cursorLeft/cursorRight/selectLeft/selectRight use. packages/editor/src/documentSelectionEdits.ts:340-351 `backspaceRangeForSelection` deletes exactly one code point. grep for grapheme/Intl.Segmenter across packages/*/src finds hits only in packages/editor/src/virtualization/virtualizedTextViewGeometry.ts:68-79,831-838 — i.e. we already segment graphemes for *measurement* but not for *movement*, so measurement and caret placement disagree.
implementationSketch: We already construct an `Intl.Segmenter({granularity:'grapheme'})` in virtualizedTextViewGeometry.ts:835; lift it into `packages/editor/src/textRanges.ts` as `previousGraphemeOffset`/`nextGraphemeOffset` operating on a line-local slice (segmenting the whole document string is not viable — slice the line via `lineRangeAtOffset`, segment, binary-search the boundary). Point `codePointOffset` in navigationTargets.ts:206 at the grapheme version. Keep backspace on a separate function: code-point delete plus a small `getOffsetBeforeLastEmojiComponent` port (needs only isEmojiModifier / VS16 / keycap / ZWJ code-point tests, ~40 lines) wired into `backspaceRangeForSelection`. Add a fallback path for environments without Intl.Segmenter using CM5's `extendingChars` regex.
verifierEvidence: Confirmed and slightly worse than claimed. /Users/shaul/Desktop/D/Editor/packages/editor/src/textRanges.ts:43-75 `previousCodePointOffset`/`nextCodePointOffset`/`codePointSizeAt` handle surrogate pairs only. /Users/shaul/Desktop/D/Editor/packages/editor/src/editor/navigation.ts is a pure re-export of textRanges, so navigationTargets.ts:206-209 `codePointOffset` is the only horizontal granularity in the editor. Deletion: /Users/shaul/Desktop/D/Editor/packages/editor/src/documentSelectionEdits.ts:326-351 has a SECOND private `previousCodePointOffset` implemented directly against the piece table (readPieceTableTextRange(snapshot, offset-2, offset)) — same surrogate-only logic, duplicated. I also checked the native path: /Users/shaul/Desktop/D/Editor/packages/editor/src/editor/inputSelectionController.ts:1128-1159 `handleBeforeInput` early-returns unless `beforeInputText(event)` is non-null, and a repo-wide grep for `getTargetRanges`/`deleteContentBackward` returns zero hits — so we never fall back to the browser's grapheme-correct deletion ranges either; Backspace always routes keymap.ts:427 -> deleteBackward -> session.backspace(). The only Segmenter in the repo is /Users/shaul/Desktop/D/Editor/packages/editor/src/virtualization/virtualizedTextViewGeometry.ts:66-79 (`GraphemeSegmenter` type), :831-838 `textPartSegments`/`createGraphemeSegmenter`, with a hand-rolled `fallbackTextSegments`/`consumeCombiningSuffix` fallback — measurement only.
verifierNotes: True gap. Note the duplication: a grapheme fix has to land in BOTH textRanges.ts (string-based, for navigation) and documentSelectionEdits.ts (piece-table-based, for backspace), or move/delete will diverge again. Cheapest correct route given our architecture: extend the existing `fallbackTextSegments`/`consumeCombiningSuffix` machinery in virtualizedTextViewGeometry.ts into a shared grapheme primitive rather than porting Monaco's GraphemeBreakTree — we already ship the Intl.Segmenter path and a fallback, they are just in the wrong package. Keeping move=grapheme / delete=grapheme-with-partial-emoji-decomposition is the Monaco nuance worth copying.

title: Word navigation has three distinct stop policies; ours is a fourth that matches none
referenceLocation: references/vscode/src/vs/editor/common/cursor/cursorWordOperations.ts:42-47 (WordNavigationType enum), :80-115 (_doFindPreviousWordOnLine), :117-141 (_findEndOfWord), :211-261 (moveWordLeft), :306-366 (moveWordRight); references/vscode/src/vs/editor/contrib/wordOperations/browser/wordOperations.ts:123-139 (cursorWordLeft = WordStartFast, bound to Ctrl/Alt+Left), :238-246 + :218-235 (cursorWordEndRight = WordEnd, bound to Ctrl/Alt+Right); references/vscode/src/vs/editor/common/core/wordCharacterClassifier.ts:18-95
mechanism: Monaco models a word as `{start, end, wordType: Regular|Separator, nextCharClass}` found by scanning one line, where every character is classified Regular / Whitespace / WordSeparator. Crucially a *run of punctuation* is itself a word (`WordType.Separator`), so `foo.bar` has three words. Four navigation policies then sit on top: **WordStart** stops at word starts; **WordStartFast** (the default for Ctrl+Left) is WordStart plus one rule — if the previous word is a single separator character immediately followed by a Regular character, skip it, so Ctrl+Left from `foo.|bar` goes to `foo` not to `.`; this rule is disabled when `hasMulticursor` is true so multiple carets do not diverge (cursorWordOperations.ts:227-240). **WordEnd** (the default for Ctrl+Right) stops *after* the last character of a word, so Ctrl+Right from `|foo bar` lands at offset 3, not 4. **WordAccessibility** skips separator-only words entirely to match screen-reader expectations. Word characters are not a Unicode property test: a cached `WordCharacterClassifier` (LRU of 10) is built from a configurable `wordSeparators` string, defaulting to ``` `~!@#$%^&*()-=+[{]}\|;:'",.<>/? ``` — everything else, including CJK and emoji, is Regular. Optional `Intl.Segmenter({granularity:'word'})` locales layer real CJK/Thai word segmentation on top (findPrevIntlWordBeforeOrAtOffset / findNextIntlWordAtOrAfterOffset, results cached per line).
whyItMatters: Concretely: in our editor Ctrl+Shift+Right on `foo bar` selects `foo ` (with the trailing space) because we always consume trailing whitespace, whereas every other editor selects `foo`. Ctrl+Left from `foo.|bar` stops on the `.` instead of jumping to `foo`. Word motion also silently walks across line breaks in ours. These are the highest-frequency keystrokes in an editor, so the mismatch is felt constantly.
ourEvidence: packages/editor/src/textRanges.ts:98-110 — `previousWordOffset` = skip spaces backward then skip one class run (≈WordStart, no fast rule); `nextWordOffset` = skip spaces, skip one class run, *then skip trailing spaces again* (≈WordStart with whitespace eaten, never WordEnd). :88-96 `characterClassAt` classifies with regexes `\s`, `[\p{L}\p{N}_]` — not a configurable separator set, so `$`, `#`, `@` are punctuation here but word characters under Monaco defaults for some languages. No `\n` guard anywhere in these loops, so motion crosses lines. packages/editor/src/editor/navigationTargets.ts:79-96 exposes exactly one left/right pair; packages/editor/src/editor/commands.ts:75-78 has only cursorWordLeft/Right + selectWordLeft/Right — no WordStart/WordEnd/Accessibility variants.
implementationSketch: Rewrite `previousWordOffset`/`nextWordOffset` in packages/editor/src/textRanges.ts to first slice the line via the existing `lineRangeAtOffset` (bounding the scan to the line and fixing the newline-crossing bug), then port `_doFindPreviousWordOnLine`/`_doFindNextWordOnLine` returning `{start,end,wordType,nextCharClass}`, and add a `WordNavigationType` parameter. Default `cursorWordLeft` to WordStartFast (passing `hasMulticursor = selections.length > 1`, available at inputSelectionController.ts:617-621) and `cursorWordRight` to WordEnd. Replace the per-character regex in `characterClassAt` with a Uint8Array-backed classifier built once from a configurable separators string (see the perf finding). Add the extra command ids to packages/editor/src/editor/commands.ts so keymaps can pick a policy per platform.
verifierEvidence: Confirmed exactly. /Users/shaul/Desktop/D/Editor/packages/editor/src/textRanges.ts:98-103 `previousWordOffset` = skipBackward(space) then skipBackward(class of preceding char); :105-110 `nextWordOffset` = skipForward(space), skipForward(class), skipForward(space) — the trailing whitespace skip makes right-motion land past the gap, matching neither WordStart nor WordEnd. :88-96 `characterClassAt` is a hardcoded `/\s/u` then `/^[\p{L}\p{N}_]$/u` (WORD_PATTERN, :8); a repo-wide grep for `wordSeparator|separators` finds only subword-separator hits in textRanges.ts:201-248 and unrelated test names — there is no configurable separator set anywhere in packages/*. `\n` classifies as 'space' via `/\s/u`, and skipBackward/skipForward (:143-164) have no line guard, so Ctrl+Left from column 0 walks into the previous line's text. Surface: navigationTargets.ts:79-96 `wordTarget` is the only word mover; commands.ts:75-78 lists exactly cursorWordLeft/Right + selectWordLeft/Right, plus deleteWordLeft/Right (commands.ts:40-41 -> editActions.ts:194-212 `deleteWordAction`, which reuses the same single policy). No WordStart/WordEnd/Accessibility variants.
verifierNotes: True. Two separable wins, and the second is much cheaper than the first: (a) a configurable `wordSeparators` string per language replacing the hardcoded WORD_PATTERN — this is what makes `$foo` in PHP/jQuery or `@media` in CSS behave right, and it is a ~20-line change to characterClassAt; (b) treating a punctuation run as its own word so `foo.bar` is three words, which our `characterClassAt` already almost gives us since 'punctuation' is a distinct class — `previousWordOffset` already stops at class transitions, so we are closer to Monaco here than the claim implies. The line-crossing bug in (\n classified as space) is the highest-value single fix in this claim and is a two-line guard.

title: Atomic soft-tab movement and tab-stop-aware backspace inside indentation
referenceLocation: references/vscode/src/vs/editor/common/cursor/cursorAtomicMoveOperations.ts:22-50 (whitespaceVisibleColumn), :62-160 (atomicPosition with Left/Right/Nearest); references/vscode/src/vs/editor/common/cursor/cursorMoveOperations.ts:41-51 (leftPositionAtomicSoftTabs), :120-130 (rightPositionAtomicSoftTabs, both gated on config.stickyTabStops and on being inside the line's indent); references/vscode/src/vs/editor/common/cursor/cursorDeleteOperations.ts:193-220 (getDeleteLeftRange, gated on config.useTabStops which is ON by default)
mechanism: Two related mechanisms. (1) `stickyTabStops`: while the caret is within a line's leading whitespace, Left/Right jump a whole `tabSize` worth of columns instead of one space. `whitespaceVisibleColumn` walks the indent once, returning the previous tab-stop position, its visible column, and the caret's visible column, bailing with -1 on any non-whitespace so the rest of the line is untouched. Going left it then re-scans forward to confirm the indent between the previous tab stop and the caret is a *full* tabSize — this is why `'      foo'` with tabSize 4 moves 6→5 (partial indent, one char) rather than 6→4. Going right it walks to `nextRenderTabStop`. `Direction.Nearest` is used by mouse hit-testing so a click inside an indent snaps to a tab stop. (2) `useTabStops` (default true, independent of stickyTabStops): backspace inside indentation deletes back to `prevIndentTabStop(visibleColumn, indentSize)` — one indent level, not one space.
whyItMatters: With soft tabs (spaces), our backspace currently removes one space at a time, so unindenting a line takes 2-4 presses instead of one — this is a daily-friction bug for any spaces-indented codebase. The Left/Right half additionally stops the caret from landing in visually meaningless positions inside indentation.
ourEvidence: grep for stickyTabStops|atomicSoftTab|atomicTab across packages/editor/src returns nothing. packages/editor/src/documentSelectionEdits.ts:340-351 `backspaceRangeForSelection` unconditionally deletes one code point back — no indent check, no tabSize. packages/editor/src/editor/editActions.ts only references tabSize at :831-853 for explicit outdent (`outdentLineEdit`/`outdentLength`), never for backspace. We do have the required primitives: `bufferColumnToVisualColumn`/`visualColumnToBufferColumn` and `view.tabSize` in packages/editor/src/virtualization/virtualizedTextViewLayout.ts:260-297.
implementationSketch: Start with the backspace half — highest value per line of code. In `backspaceRangeForSelection` (documentSelectionEdits.ts:340), when the selection is collapsed, read the line via `lineRangeAtOffset`, compute `firstNonWhitespaceIndex`; if the caret is at or before it, convert caret→visible column with the existing `bufferColumnToVisualColumn`, round down to the previous multiple of indentSize, convert back, and delete that range. Needs `tabSize`/`indentSize` threaded into `SelectionEditResult` options (the shape at documentSelectionEdits.ts:40 already carries `tabSize?`). Then port `AtomicTabMoveOperations.atomicPosition` verbatim (~90 lines, pure string+number, trivially unit-testable) and call it from `horizontalTarget` in navigationTargets.ts:58 behind an option, plus `Direction.Nearest` from `textOffsetFromPoint` in the mouse path.
verifierEvidence: Confirmed. Repo-wide grep for `stickyTabStops|atomicSoftTab|atomicTab` returns nothing. Backspace: documentSelectionEdits.ts:340-351 `backspaceRangeForSelection` unconditionally returns {previousCodePointOffset, startOffset} with no indent or tabSize input; the only tabSize consumers in packages/editor/src are documentSession.ts:57/315/804 (outdentSelection), documentSelectionEdits.ts:132/255-271 (`outdentLength`, which already implements 'delete back to the previous tab stop' — `while (spaces < tabSize && text[spaces] === ' ')`), the virtualization layer, and displayTransforms.ts:212-288. Primitives all exist: displayTransforms.ts:221-253 `bufferColumnToVisualColumn`/`visualColumnToBufferColumn` are tab-aware and pure, and editActions.ts:1191 `firstNonWhitespaceOffset` already computes the indent boundary for line ops. Also confirmed: nothing in the horizontal path (navigationTargets.ts:59-77 `horizontalTarget`) consults tabSize.
verifierNotes: True, but split it. The backspace-to-previous-tab-stop half is high value / low effort: `outdentLength` in documentSelectionEdits.ts:267-271 is literally the algorithm already, it just is not reachable from backspace — the change is a caret-is-in-leading-whitespace guard in `backspaceRangeForSelection` reusing it. The `stickyTabStops` arrow-movement half is off by default even in Monaco and is a genuine niche preference; I would implement it only behind an option, or not at all. Worth flagging the deeper design point: our horizontal motion has no access to view/tabSize at all (navigationTargets.ts:19-23 NavigationTargetView exposes offsetAtLineBoundary/offsetByDisplayRows/pageRowDelta/visualColumnForOffset but nothing indentation-related), so the arrow half is a wider plumbing change than the backspace half.

title: Multi-cursor merge rules: touching vs overlapping, direction preservation, and last-added priority
referenceLocation: references/vscode/src/vs/editor/common/cursor/cursorCollection.ts:158-252 (normalize), :19-32 (cursors[0] is primary, lastAddedCursorIndex), :140-142 (killSecondaryCursors keeps cursors[0]), :144-148 (_addSecondaryCursor updates lastAddedCursorIndex), :157-160 (_removeSecondaryCursor shifts it)
mechanism: Monaco's `normalize()` sorts a copy of the cursors by range start and merges neighbours, but the merge predicate is asymmetric: if either selection is empty, merge when they merely *touch* (`nextStart.isBeforeOrEqual(currentEnd)`); if both are non-empty, merge only on strict *overlap* (`isBefore`). Two adjacent non-empty selections therefore survive as two cursors. When a merge does happen, the surviving state is chosen by original cursor index — the lower-indexed (older) cursor is the 'winner' and its LTR/RTL direction is kept, *except* when the loser is `lastAddedCursorIndex`, in which case the last-added cursor's direction wins and `lastAddedCursorIndex` is transferred to the survivor. Sort order never becomes identity order: `cursors[0]` stays the primary cursor, is what reveal/scroll follows, and is the one that survives Escape (`killSecondaryCursors`).
whyItMatters: Ours merges any two selections that touch, so Ctrl+D-selecting two adjacent identical tokens (`abab` → `ab|ab`) collapses them into one selection instead of two cursors, and typing then replaces the whole run. Merging also throws away direction and goal column, so after two cursors collide, Shift+Arrow reverses meaning and Up/Down loses the column. And because we treat `selections[0]` (document order) as primary, Escape from a multi-cursor set keeps the topmost cursor rather than the one the user started from, and reveal jumps to the top of the document.
ourEvidence: packages/editor/src/selections.ts:209-210 — `shouldMergeRanges = right.start <= left.end`, a single unconditional touching test with no empty/non-empty distinction. :233-250 `mergeResolvedSelections` hard-codes `reversed: false` and `goal: SelectionGoal.none()`, discarding both. :200-207 `compareResolvedSelections` sorts by offset and ties on `id.localeCompare`, and :275 returns the sorted array, so document order becomes cursor order. There is no `lastAdded` concept anywhere. packages/editor/src/documentSession.ts:705-710 and :1013-1018 collapse to `normalized.selections[0]` — the topmost, not the original.
implementationSketch: In packages/editor/src/selections.ts, change `shouldMergeRanges` to take both resolved selections and apply the empty/non-empty split. In `mergeResolvedSelections`, keep the winner's `reversed` and `goal` instead of resetting them. Add an `order`/creation-index field to `Selection<T>` (or reuse a monotonic counter in the existing `createSelectionIdFactory` at :73) so `normalizeSelections` can sort for merging but restore creation order for the returned array, keeping index 0 = primary; then `documentSession.ts:705/1013` collapse to the true primary for free. A `lastAddedIndex` on `SelectionSet` set by `addSelection` (inputSelectionController.ts:931) gives the direction-priority rule.
verifierEvidence: Confirmed on every point. /Users/shaul/Desktop/D/Editor/packages/editor/src/selections.ts:209-210 `shouldMergeRanges = right.start <= left.end` — one unconditional touching test, no empty/non-empty branch, so two adjacent non-empty selections (e.g. word-select `foo` then `bar` in `foobar`) collapse into one. :233-250 `mergeResolvedSelections` builds the survivor with `goal: SelectionGoal.none(), reversed: false` — direction and goal column are both dropped; note that :226-232 `normalizeResolvedSelection` (the non-merging path) DOES preserve reversed and goal, so the loss is specific to merges. :200-207 `compareResolvedSelections` sorts by startOffset, then endOffset, then `id.localeCompare`, and :275 returns that order, so document order is the only order. No `lastAdded`/anchor-cursor concept anywhere — the only `primary*` symbols in the repo are `primarySelectionHeadOffset` (inputSelectionController.ts:1458) and find's `primarySelection` (packages/find/src/findController.ts:492), both of which just mean 'index 0'. Escape behaviour confirmed at documentSession.ts:700-712 and :1008-1022 — both `clearSecondarySelections` implementations keep `normalized.selections[0]`, the topmost, so alt-clicking a cursor below and pressing Escape teleports you up.
verifierNotes: True and this one has a user-visible bug attached, not just a fidelity difference: Escape after adding a cursor below jumps the caret to the top of the document region rather than back to where you were. Three independent fixes, all cheap and all in selections.ts: (1) make `shouldMergeRanges` take both ranges' collapsed-ness and require strict overlap when both are non-empty; (2) in `mergeResolvedSelections`, take reversed/goal from whichever input's head survives as the merged head instead of hardcoding false/none; (3) add a `lastAddedIndex` alongside the selection set so Escape and Cmd+D anchor on it. (3) is the one with real reach — Cmd+D (claim 10) depends on it too.

title: Column (box) selection: a persistent from/to visual-column rectangle, driven by mouse and keyboard
referenceLocation: references/vscode/src/vs/editor/common/cursor/cursorColumnSelection.ts:12-75 (columnSelect), :77-90 (columnSelectLeft), :86-105 (columnSelectRight scans for max visual column), :107-118 (columnSelectUp/Down with isPaged); references/vscode/src/vs/editor/common/cursor/cursor.ts:39,130,137-139,285-299,395 (_columnSelectData lifecycle, getCursorColumnSelectData synthesising isReal:false state from the primary cursor, invalidation on any edit); references/vscode/src/vs/editor/browser/view/viewController.ts:217-310 (dispatchMouse: middle button, alt+shift+click, alt+drag, and the `columnSelection` option all route to _columnSelect)
mechanism: Column selection is not N independent cursors; it is a single `IColumnSelectData` rectangle `{fromViewLineNumber, fromViewVisualColumn, toViewLineNumber, toViewVisualColumn}` stored on the cursor controller, from which the cursor list is *derived* on every change. `ColumnSelection.columnSelect` walks each line in the range, converts both visual columns to real columns with `columnFromVisibleColumn` (tab-aware), converts back to visible columns, and drops lines whose entire content falls outside the rectangle's column band — so short lines contribute no cursor rather than a clamped one, unless *every* line is short, in which case it falls back to a caret at each line end. The keyboard commands mutate only the `to` corner of the stored rectangle, which is why Ctrl+Shift+Alt+Right can push past the end of short lines and later re-acquire them (`columnSelectRight` computes the max visual column across the whole band to know when to stop). `_columnSelectData` is nulled by any edit (`_interpretCommandResult`, cursor.ts:395) and re-synthesised from the primary cursor with `isReal: false` when absent.
whyItMatters: Box selection over columnar data (aligned assignments, CSV-ish blocks, log columns) is one of the two or three reasons people reach for multi-cursor at all, and it is the case pure multi-cursor cannot express because short lines must be *skipped*, not clamped. We have neither the mouse nor the keyboard entry point.
ourEvidence: packages/editor/src/editor/commands.ts:1-90 has no column-select command of any kind. packages/editor/src/editor/inputSelectionController.ts:915-918 — the only altKey handling in mousedown is `addCursorAtOffset`; alt+drag is never distinguished from a plain drag (`startMouseSelectionDrag`, :938-955). No middle-button branch. mouseSelection.ts (45 lines) is only auto-scroll math.
implementationSketch: The primitives exist: `visualColumnForOffset` and `offsetForViewportColumn` (packages/editor/src/virtualization/virtualizedTextViewLayout.ts:260-297) are exactly Monaco's `visibleColumnFromColumn`/`columnFromVisibleColumn`, and `rowForOffset` gives display lines. Add a `columnSelect: ColumnSelectData | null` field alongside `mouseSelectionDrag` in inputSelectionController.ts, cleared in `applySessionChange` on any edit. Port `ColumnSelection.columnSelect` (~60 lines) mapping (row, visualColumn) pairs through the two existing helpers, and have it produce a `setSelections` payload. Wire the entry points in `handleMouseDown` (:891-921): alt+drag and middle button start a column drag; add `columnSelectLeft/Right/Up/Down/PageUp/PageDown` command ids that mutate only the stored `to` corner.
verifierEvidence: Confirmed. Repo-wide case-insensitive grep for `columnSelect|columnSelection|boxSelect|rectangularSelect|blockSelect` across packages/**/*.ts returns zero hits. commands.ts:1-89 (full EditorCommandId union) contains no column command. inputSelectionController.ts:891-921 `handleMouseDown` branches on detail>=4 / 3 / 2 / `event.altKey`, and the altKey branch calls `addCursorAtOffset` (:922-940) — alt+drag is indistinguishable from a plain drag, which then goes to `startMouseSelectionDrag` (:942-958) storing a scalar `MouseSelectionDrag {anchorOffset, headOffset, clientX, clientY}` (mouseSelection.ts:4-9). No middle-button branch anywhere (`event.button !== 0` returns early at :925 and :943). mouseSelection.ts is 45 lines of auto-scroll math only.
verifierNotes: True gap, and genuinely worth it — column selection is one of the few remaining things people leave an editor over. But be honest about effort: the win in Monaco's design is that the rectangle is the source of truth and the N cursors are DERIVED on every change, which means our `SelectionSet` would need a parallel 'column select data' field on the session that survives normalization (selections.ts:36-40 SelectionSet has only {selections, normalized, normalizedFor}). We do already have both halves of the hard math — displayTransforms.ts:221-253 bufferColumnToVisualColumn/visualColumnToBufferColumn is exactly Monaco's columnFromVisibleColumn, and virtualizedTextViewRows.ts:1119-1124 already picks the fast vs estimated path. So the geometry is free; the state plumbing is the cost.

title: Cursor undo/redo as an independent bounded stack
referenceLocation: references/vscode/src/vs/editor/contrib/cursorUndo/browser/cursorUndo.ts:16-35 (CursorState.equals), :37-43 (StackElement also captures scrollTop/scrollLeft), :66-93 (recording: cleared on model or content change, records `e.oldSelections` only when `oldModelVersionId === modelVersionId`, dedupes against the stack top, capped at 50), :96-120 (cursorUndo/cursorRedo push the current state onto the opposite stack), :113-121 (_applyState restores selections *and* scroll position under an `_isCursorUndoRedo` reentrancy guard)
mechanism: A separate 50-deep undo stack that records only pure cursor movements — the `oldModelVersionId === modelVersionId` test is what excludes selection changes caused by edits, and any content change wipes both stacks so cursor-undo can never fight document-undo. Each entry stores scroll position too, so Cmd+U returns you to where you were *looking*, not just where the caret was. The reentrancy flag stops the restore from recording itself.
whyItMatters: After a Ctrl+D run, a Go-to-Definition, or an accidental Ctrl+Home in a large file, there is currently no way back to the previous selection state except manual navigation. This is a small, self-contained feature with an outsized 'I can experiment safely' payoff, and it composes especially well with our multi-cursor and find features.
ourEvidence: grep for cursorUndo across packages/editor/src returns nothing; packages/editor/src/editor/commands.ts:2-3 has only `undo`/`redo`. packages/editor/src/history.ts (113 lines) stores `selections` inside each *document* history entry (:3,15,49,87,105) — i.e. selection is restored as a side effect of text undo, which is the opposite of what this feature needs.
implementationSketch: New file packages/editor/src/editor/cursorHistory.ts holding two arrays of `{selections: EditorSelectionRange[], scrollTop, scrollLeft}`. Hook it in `applySessionChange` (packages/editor/src/editor/Editor.ts / inputSelectionController.ts) — we already pass a timing/source name per call, so 'was this an edit or a pure selection change?' is answerable without version-id comparison: clear both stacks on any change whose `edits.length > 0`, push the previous selections otherwise. Add `cursorUndo`/`cursorRedo` to commands.ts and bind Cmd+U in keymap.ts alongside the existing entries at :434.
verifierEvidence: Confirmed. Grep for `cursorUndo|cursorRedo|selectionUndo|selectionHistory` across all packages returns zero hits. commands.ts:2-3 has only 'undo'|'redo'. /Users/shaul/Desktop/D/Editor/packages/editor/src/history.ts:1-5 defines `EditorHistoryEntry {snapshot, selections, transaction}` and :39-52 `commitEditorHistory` pushes the PREVIOUS snapshot+selections as one unit — selection is strictly a passenger of document history, restored only as a side effect of text undo. There is no version-id concept to distinguish 'selection changed because the user moved' from 'selection changed because an edit moved it'; documentSession.ts tracks `this.revision` (:452-458) but nothing compares it across a selection change.
verifierNotes: True gap but I'd rank it lowest-value of the missing items. It is a real, well-liked Monaco feature (Cmd+U), and the mechanism is genuinely clever — the `oldModelVersionId === modelVersionId` test is what makes it not fight document undo, and storing scroll position is what makes it feel right. We have `revision` on the session already, so that test is available to us cheaply. Keeping it, but as a low-priority nice-to-have rather than a correctness fix; if effort is constrained, claims 1, 7, 12 and 13 all beat it.

title: Mouse dispatch matrix: shift-click extend, and word/line-granularity drag via a Range-valued anchor
referenceLocation: references/vscode/src/vs/editor/browser/view/viewController.ts:217-310 (full dispatch matrix: middle button, gutter-started line drags, count>=4 select-all, count 3 line/lineDrag, count 2 word/wordDrag/lastCursorWordSelect, single click with multicursor modifier, alt+shift = columnSelect); references/vscode/src/vs/editor/browser/controller/mouseHandler.ts:459-500 (drag-and-drop of an existing selection is preferred over re-selecting; `_dispatchMouse(position, e.shiftKey, ...)` — shiftKey *is* inSelectionMode); references/vscode/src/vs/editor/common/cursorCommon.ts:342-399 (SingleCursorState.selectionStart is a **Range**, selectionStartKind Simple|Word|Line, and _computeSelection picks whichever end of that anchor range is away from the position); references/vscode/src/vs/editor/common/cursor/cursorWordOperations.ts:741-820 (WordOperations.word: first entry sets a Word-kind anchor; subsequent inSelectionMode calls snap the moving end to whole-word boundaries and flip which anchor end is used)
mechanism: The decisive design choice is that the anchor is a *Range*, not a point, tagged with a granularity kind. Double-click sets `selectionStart` to the whole word with `SelectionStartKind.Word`; every subsequent drag position is then snapped to word boundaries and `_computeSelection` picks the far end of the anchor range, which is what makes double-click-and-drag select whole words in both directions and never shrink below the original word. Triple-click does the same with a line-sized anchor. Shift+click is not a special case at all — it is simply `inSelectionMode = e.shiftKey` fed into the same dispatch, so shift+click after a double-click extends *by word*.
whyItMatters: Three very ordinary gestures are unavailable in our editor today: shift+click to extend a selection, double-click-then-drag to select by word, and triple-click-then-drag to select by line. Shift+click in particular is muscle memory for selecting a large region without dragging through a scrolling viewport.
ourEvidence: packages/editor/src/editor/inputSelectionController.ts:891-921 `handleMouseDown` — branches only on `event.detail` (>=4, 3, 2) and `event.altKey`; a grep for `shiftKey` across packages/editor/src/editor/*.ts (only keymap.ts hits) confirms no shift handling in the mouse path. The detail===2 and detail===3 branches `return` immediately after `selectWordAtOffset`/`selectLineAtOffset` (:1103-1111, :1095-1101), so no drag monitor is started at all. packages/editor/src/selections.ts:24-30 — `Selection<T>` carries `start`/`end`/`reversed`; the anchor is recoverable only as a single offset (`anchorOffset`, :181-182), so a word- or line-sized anchor is not representable. packages/editor/src/editor/mouseSelection.ts is 45 lines of auto-scroll math only.
implementationSketch: Extend `MouseSelectionDrag` (mouseSelection.ts:4-9) from `anchorOffset: number` to `anchor: {start, end}` plus `granularity: 'char'|'word'|'line'`. In `updateMouseSelectionFromDragPoint` (:1006-1020), expand the pointer offset with the existing `wordRangeAtOffset`/`lineRangeAtOffset` (textRanges.ts:35-41, :112-131) when granularity is word/line, then union with the anchor range and set head to the far end. Have the detail===2/3 branches fall through into `startMouseSelectionDrag` with the matching granularity instead of returning. Add a shift branch at the top of `handleMouseDown` that keeps the current selection's anchor and only moves the head. Longer term, promoting `SelectionGoal`-style metadata to a `selectionStartKind` on `Selection<T>` would also make keyboard shift+arrow after a double-click behave correctly.
verifierEvidence: Confirmed, and the shift-click part is stronger than claimed: a repo-wide grep for `shiftKey` finds hits ONLY in packages/panes/src/index.ts:238, packages/find/src/findWidget.ts:207-268, and packages/editor/test/editor.test.ts — zero occurrences in packages/editor/src at all (the former packages/diff/src/DiffView.ts:1220-1221 hits went away with `DiffView`), including keymap.ts (which encodes shift via `key('L', {mod: true, shift: true})` string descriptors, keymap.ts:507). So shift-click does not extend the selection anywhere in the editor. Granularity drag: inputSelectionController.ts:906-919 — the detail===3 and detail===2 branches call `selectLineAtOffset` (:1095-1101) / `selectWordAtOffset` (:1103-1111), both of which route to `selectRange` (:1113-1126) and return with no mousemove/mouseup listeners attached, so double-click-drag and triple-click-drag do nothing. Anchor shape: mouseSelection.ts:4-9 `MouseSelectionDrag.anchorOffset` is a scalar number, and selections.ts:24-30 `Selection<T>` has no granularity tag — a word- or line-sized anchor is not representable.
verifierNotes: True and this is the highest value-per-effort item in the whole list. Shift-click alone is table stakes that we simply do not have — every native text control and every editor does it. The Range-valued-anchor design is the right thing to copy verbatim: widening `MouseSelectionDrag` from `anchorOffset: number` to `anchor: {start, end, kind: 'char'|'word'|'line'}` and snapping the drag head through the existing `wordRangeAtOffset`/`lineRangeAtOffset` (textRanges.ts:34-40, :112-131) gets shift-click, double-click-drag and triple-click-drag from one change, because all three reduce to 'anchor is a range, head is snapped to the same granularity, pick the far end'. Note the drag path also calls `session.materializeFullText()` per double/triple click (:1098, :1106) — see claim 13.

title: Word-part (subword) motion clamped between the word-start and word-end candidates
referenceLocation: references/vscode/src/vs/editor/common/cursor/cursorWordOperations.ts:845-853 (moveWordPartLeft = max of three candidates), :855-863 (moveWordPartRight = min of three candidates), :825-833 / :835-843 (deleteWordPartLeft/Right use the same trick on Ranges via Range.compareRangesUsingEnds/Starts), :264-303 (_moveWordPartLeft: pure camelCase/snake_case/kebab-case scan that stops at column 1 and refuses to leave the line, with the `HTTPResponse` acronym rule at :291-301)
mechanism: Monaco never lets the raw subword scanner decide alone. `moveWordPartLeft` computes three positions — `moveWordLeft(WordStart)`, `moveWordLeft(WordEnd)`, and the raw `_moveWordPartLeft` — sorts them with `Position.compare`, and takes the **last** (nearest to the caret going left); `moveWordPartRight` takes the **first** going right. The raw scanner therefore only ever gets to *shorten* a move that word navigation already bounded; it can never carry the caret past a word boundary, past whitespace, or (because `_moveWordPartLeft` returns column 1 / maxColumn at the line edges) across a line break. The delete variants apply the identical clamp to Ranges. This is a very cheap way to get correct subword behaviour without the subword scanner having to understand whitespace, punctuation, or newlines at all.
whyItMatters: Our subword scanner treats every non-alphanumeric character — including `\n` — as a separator to be skipped, so Alt+Ctrl+Right from the end of a line silently jumps to the next line's first subword, and from a position before whitespace it skips the gap and lands at the *end* of the next word rather than its start. Users lose their place, and it makes subword motion unusable for careful editing.
ourEvidence: packages/editor/src/textRanges.ts:196-233 — `nextWordPartOffset`/`previousWordPartOffset` run standalone with no word-boundary clamp. :248-252 `isSubwordSeparator` is `!/[\p{L}\p{N}]/u.test(char)`, which is true for `\n`, and both functions loop over separators unconditionally (:202, :222) so line breaks are traversed. Commands exist (packages/editor/src/editor/commands.ts:61-64, navigationTargets.ts:98-115) but there is no `deleteWordPartLeft`/`deleteWordPartRight` counterpart in commands.ts. Our acronym rule at textRanges.ts:236-246 is already equivalent to Monaco's.
implementationSketch: Once `previousWordOffset`/`nextWordOffset` take a `WordNavigationType` (see the word-navigation finding), wrap the existing calls in navigationTargets.ts:98-115: `previousWordPartOffset → Math.max(previousWordOffset(WordStart), previousWordOffset(WordEnd), rawPrevious)` and the symmetric `Math.min` going right. That is ~6 lines and fixes both the newline crossing and the overshoot without touching the subword scanner. Add `deleteWordPartLeft/Right` to commands.ts applying the same clamp to the delete ranges.
verifierEvidence: Confirmed. textRanges.ts:196-233 `nextWordPartOffset`/`previousWordPartOffset` take only (text, offset) and never consult `previousWordOffset`/`nextWordOffset` — no clamp. :248-252 `isSubwordSeparator` is `!/[\p{L}\p{N}]/u.test(char)`, true for '\n', and the separator-skipping loops at :202 and :222 are unbounded, so Ctrl+Alt+Left from a line start walks into the previous line. navigationTargets.ts:98-115 `wordPartTarget` passes the raw scanner result straight through. Commands exist and are complete on the motion side — commands.ts:61-64 cursorWordPartLeft/Right/LeftSelect/RightSelect, wired at navigationTargets.ts:44-47 — but there is no deleteWordPartLeft/Right in the commands.ts union (:38-41 has only deleteWordLeft/deleteWordRight) and none in editActions.ts:9-10/145-146. Our acronym rule at textRanges.ts:236-246 `startsSubword` (HTTP|Response via `isUpper(previous) && isLower(text[index+1])`) is behaviourally equivalent to Monaco's, and is covered by /Users/shaul/Desktop/D/Editor/packages/editor/test/wordPart.test.ts.
verifierNotes: True. The clamp is the valuable half and it is nearly free for us: `wordPartTarget` in navigationTargets.ts:98-115 already has `context.text` and `context.resolved.headOffset`, so computing previousWordOffset/nextWordOffset alongside the raw result and taking min/max is a handful of lines — and it fixes the line-crossing bug as a side effect, since word motion would bound it. deleteWordPartLeft/Right is a straightforward addition to editActions.ts mirroring `deleteWordAction` (:194-212). Both worth doing.

title: Smart-select as a ranked ladder of ranges, not a single tree walk
referenceLocation: references/vscode/src/vs/editor/contrib/smartSelect/browser/smartSelect.ts:33-52 (SelectionRanges.mov skips ranges equal to the current one), :74-127 (run: computes the ladder once, prepends the live selection, and drops the whole state on any cursor move via onDidChangeCursorPosition), :245-276 (sort + keep only ranges that strictly contain the previous one), :277-300 (synthesised 'line without leading/trailing whitespace' and 'full line' steps inserted whenever a step crosses onto a new line); references/vscode/src/vs/editor/contrib/smartSelect/browser/wordSelections.ts:31-72 (_addInWordRanges: subword step from camelCase/snake_case/kebab-case), :74-79 (word step), :81-89 (whitespace-only-line step); references/vscode/src/vs/editor/contrib/smartSelect/browser/bracketSelections.ts:13-27,31-75,77-125 (bracket provider yields *both* inner and outer bracket ranges, and time-slices with _maxDuration=30ms across _maxRounds=2 so huge files never block)
mechanism: Providers each contribute an unordered bucket of candidate ranges; the framework filters to ranges containing the caret, sorts them, then keeps only a strictly increasing containment chain (dropping duplicates and equal ranges), and finally interpolates two synthetic steps — 'the line's content without leading/trailing whitespace' and 'the whole line' — at every point where the chain jumps to a new line. The resulting ladder is computed once and cached with an index; Expand/Shrink just move the index, and `mov` skips steps that would not visibly change the selection. The state is invalidated by *cursor movement*, not by document version, and the bracket provider is written to yield inner-then-outer so `(a, b)` gives you the contents before the parens.
whyItMatters: Our expand/shrink jumps straight from the caret to the smallest named tree-sitter node, so the first press on `fooBar` selects the whole identifier — there is no subword step, no 'line without indentation' step, and no expansion at all in a buffer with no grammar (plain text, markdown, an unsupported language). Shrink is also only guarded by snapshot version, so clicking elsewhere and pressing Shrink pops a stale stack and teleports the selection.
ourEvidence: packages/tree-sitter/src/structuralSelection.ts:45-55 (expand) and :57-71 (shrink) — a single tree-sitter provider, one range per press. packages/tree-sitter/src/treeSitter/treeSitter.worker.ts:1585-1615 — `expandedRangeAt` walks to `containingNamedNode`, so the ladder is exactly the named-node chain: no subword, no word, no trivia steps. :1600-1603 requires a parsed layer, so no grammar means no expansion. structuralSelection.ts:147-156 `rangesFromShrinkState` validates only `snapshotVersion !== options.snapshotVersion` — nothing invalidates on cursor movement. :136-142 rebuilds selections with `reversed: false`, losing direction.
implementationSketch: Keep the tree-sitter worker as one provider but move ladder assembly to the editor package: a `selectionRangeProviders` array where the tree-sitter backend is one entry and a pure-text `WordSelectionRangeProvider` (port of wordSelections.ts, ~60 lines, reusing our `wordRangeAtOffset` at textRanges.ts:112) is another that always works. Add the containment-chain filter and the two synthetic line steps from smartSelect.ts:245-300 — they cost nothing and are what makes the ladder feel smooth. Invalidate the cached stack in structuralSelection.ts on any selection change rather than on snapshot version, mirroring the `_ignoreSelection` guard so our own writes do not self-invalidate.
verifierEvidence: Confirmed, plus one finding the survey missed. structuralSelection.ts:38-42 `selectTreeSitterToken`, :45-55 `expandTreeSitterSelection`, :57-70 `shrinkTreeSitterSelection` — one tree-sitter provider, one range per press, stack kept in `TreeSitterSelectionExpansionState`. treeSitter.worker.ts:1585-1592 `selectionRangeForAction` dispatches to `tokenRangeAt` (:1594-1598, `descendantForIndex` — so we DO have one sub-named-node 'token' step, slightly better than the claim's 'exactly the named-node chain') or `expandedRangeAt` (:1600-1603) -> `containingNamedNode` (:1605-1614). No subword, word, line-content or whole-line steps. :1567-1573 returns `staleSelectionResult` when no parsed layer is cached, so no grammar means no expansion at all. structuralSelection.ts:147-156 `rangesFromShrinkState` invalidates only on `snapshotVersion` mismatch — moving the caret does not reset the ladder. :136-142 `selectionSetFromRanges` hardcodes `reversed: false`. NEW: grep for `expandTreeSitterSelection|shrinkTreeSitterSelection|selectTreeSitterToken` outside the defining file returns hits ONLY in packages/tree-sitter/test/treeSitter-workerClient.browser.test.ts — and there is no expandSelection/smartSelect/shrinkSelection command id anywhere in packages/*/src. The feature is not reachable from any keybinding or command.
verifierNotes: True, and worse than reported: the machinery is orphaned — no command id, no keymap entry, only tests call it. Ranking the work: (1) wire it to a command at all; (2) the synthetic word/line-content/whole-line steps, which are what make Cmd+Shift+Right useful in a file with no grammar and are pure string work we can do with the existing wordRangeAtOffset/lineRangeAtOffset; (3) invalidate the ladder on caret movement; (4) preserve `reversed`. The provider-bucket architecture (unordered candidates -> filter -> sort -> strictly-increasing chain) is worth adopting because it is what lets LSP selectionRange, tree-sitter, and the synthetic steps coexist — we have an LSP package that could contribute to it.

title: Cmd+D from a collapsed caret is whole-word and case-sensitive, and searches from the last-added selection
referenceLocation: references/vscode/src/vs/editor/contrib/multicursor/browser/multicursor.ts:276-325 (MultiCursorSession.create: `if (selections.length === 1 && selections[0].isEmpty()) { isDisconnectedFromFindController = true; wholeWord = true; matchCase = true; }`, and the empty-selection branch expands to `getConfiguredWordAtPosition`), :368-383 (_getNextMatch: `currentMatch` is consumed once so the first Cmd+D selects the word under the caret rather than jumping, then search resumes from `allSelections[allSelections.length - 1].getEndPosition()` — the **last added** selection, not the last in document order), :335-347 / :387-399 (addSelectionToNext/Previous), :440-452 (selectAll)
mechanism: The session captures search settings at creation time and remembers whether it owns them. Starting from a bare caret it forces wholeWord+matchCase and disconnects from the find widget's state, so Cmd+D on `foo` will not match the `foo` inside `foobar` or `Foo`. `currentMatch` makes the first press a pure 'select the word under the caret' with no search at all. Subsequent presses anchor the search at the end of the *most recently added* selection, which is what makes Cmd+D feel like it walks forward from where you last were even when earlier cursors sit later in the document.
whyItMatters: In our editor, placing the caret in `id` and pressing Cmd+D repeatedly picks up `id` inside `width`, `valid`, `hidden` — the classic wrong-rename accident, because the very next thing users do is type over all the cursors. This is a small fix with a large blast radius avoided.
ourEvidence: packages/editor/src/editor/occurrences.ts:99-115 `findExactOccurrenceFrom` uses plain `text.indexOf(query)` with no boundary test; :45-58 `findAllExactOccurrences` likewise. :60-76 `findNextExactOccurrence` computes `searchStart = selected.reduce((o, r) => Math.max(o, r.end), 0)` — the maximum end across *all* selections, i.e. document order, not the last added. :20-28 `getOccurrenceQuery` takes `selections.find(s => !s.collapsed)` — the first non-collapsed in document order — as the query source. We already have the needed predicate: packages/editor/src/textRanges.ts:133-141 `isWholeWordRange`, used by packages/find/src/search.ts:205 but never by occurrences.ts.
implementationSketch: Thread a `{wholeWord: boolean; matchCase: boolean}` session state through `addNextExactOccurrence` (packages/editor/src/editor/inputSelectionController.ts:1382-1411), set to `{true, true}` on the branch that already detects `resolved.length === 1 && primary.collapsed` (:1391), and reset it when the user starts from a real selection. In `findExactOccurrenceFrom` (occurrences.ts:99), reject candidates failing `isWholeWordRange(text, range)` when the flag is set. Change `searchStart` to derive from a tracked last-added selection index rather than `Math.max` over ends — the same `lastAdded` field proposed for the merge-rules finding.
verifierEvidence: Confirmed, with one correction in our favour. occurrences.ts:99-115 `findExactOccurrenceFrom` and :44-58 `findAllExactOccurrences` use bare `text.indexOf(query)` — no word-boundary test, so Cmd+D on `foo` matches inside `foobar`. Case sensitivity is implicit (indexOf), so that half is already correct by accident. :60-76 `findNextExactOccurrence` computes `searchStart = selected.reduce((o, r) => Math.max(o, r.end), 0)` — max end over all selections. :20-28 `getOccurrenceQuery` takes the first non-collapsed selection in document order. So the last-added-anchor primitive already exists and is used; Cmd+D just does not call it. Also confirmed: inputSelectionController.ts:1425-1450 `selectCurrentWordForOccurrence` makes the first Cmd+D from a bare caret a pure word-select with no search, matching Monaco's `currentMatch`. The needed boundary predicate exists at textRanges.ts:133-141 `isWholeWordRange` and is used by packages/find/src/search.ts but never by occurrences.ts.

The remaining work is genuinely small: pass a wholeWord flag into `findExactOccurrenceFrom` gated on 'the session started from a collapsed caret' and filtered through the existing `isWholeWordRange`, and switch `addNextExactOccurrence` from `resolved[0]`/`findNextExactOccurrence` to `resolved.at(-1)`/`findNextExactOccurrenceFromRange` — i.e. make it match the sibling function 30 lines above it. title: Auto-closing: token-aware quote suppression via a 'neutral character' probe, and multi-cursor surround

title: Clipboard carries no editor metadata, so multi-cursor copy/paste degenerates into one blob
referenceLocation: vscode: src/vs/editor/browser/controller/editContext/clipboardUtils.ts:31-71 (generateDataToCopy), :78-99 (InMemoryClipboardMetadataManager), :131-159 (ClipboardEventUtils get/setTextData, 'vscode-editor-data' MIME), :22-29 (Firefox \r\n normalisation); src/vs/editor/common/cursor/cursorTypeEditOperations.ts:654-705 (PasteOperation._distributePasteToCursors / _distributedPaste); src/vs/editor/common/viewModel/viewModelImpl.ts:998-1049 (getPlainTextToCopy); codemirror5/src/input/input.js:14-21 (lastCopied), :30-42 (multiPaste distribution)

CM5 does the same thing more cheaply with a module-level `lastCopied = {lineWise, text: [...]}` compared by `text.join('\n') == inserted`, and also supports N cursors being an integer multiple of the copied fragment count (`sel.ranges.length % lastCopied.text.length == 0`).
