title: Diff-based input deduction as the robust fallback, instead of a keydown timing race
referenceLocation: vscode: src/vs/editor/browser/controller/editContext/textArea/textAreaEditContextState.ts:117-179 (TextAreaState.deduceInput — commonPrefix/commonSuffix clamped by the selection), :181-227 (deduceAndroidCompositionInput), :50-63 (readFromTextArea carrying newlineCountBeforeSelection forward); src/vs/editor/browser/controller/editContext/textArea/textAreaEditContextInput.ts:322-364 (onInput: ignore lone high surrogates and 0x7f but keep them for next time; route insertFromPaste to onPaste), :221-262 (macOS long-press + Android compositionstart special cases), :445-462 (onBlur during composition fires an artificial compositionend)
mechanism: Monaco never guesses what a keystroke meant. It writes a known string+selection into the textarea, and on every `input` event diffs the new textarea state against the remembered one: `prefixLength = min(commonPrefixLength, prevSelStart, curSelStart)`, `suffixLength = min(commonSuffixLength, prevLen-prevSelEnd, curLen-curSelEnd)`, yielding `{text, replacePrevCharCnt, replaceNextCharCnt, positionDelta}`. Clamping the common prefix/suffix by the selection bounds is the subtle part — it prevents a repeated character adjacent to the caret from being absorbed into the prefix. The same primitive expresses ordinary typing, composition replacement, dead keys, autocorrect-style multi-character replacements and Android's word-level suggestion edits (which is why `deduceAndroidCompositionInput` exists as a variant that also computes `replaceNextCharCnt`). Guard rails: a lone high surrogate or 0x7f is dropped but deliberately left in the textarea so the next event completes it; a blur during composition synthesises a compositionend so the editor doesn't get stuck composing.
whyItMatters: Our current design instead races: on keydown it optimistically waits for a native `input` event and, if none arrives, replays the guessed character (`native-input-wait-started` -> `native-input-missing`). title: ZoneWidget: view zone reserves whitespace, the DOM lives in a stable overlay widget driven by onDomNodeTop — our block-row DOM is destroyed on scroll recycle
referenceLocation: references/vscode/src/vs/editor/contrib/zoneWidget/browser/zoneWidget.ts:385-460 (_showImpl: creates an *empty* viewZoneDomNode, registers it as a view zone, then registers `this.domNode` as an OverlayWidgetDelegate), :288-300 (_onViewZoneTop sets domNode.style.top, _onViewZoneHeight re-lays out the body); references/vscode/src/vs/editor/browser/viewParts/viewZones/viewZones.ts:357-410 (render: every zone node stays in the DOM forever, only top/height/display are updated, plus onDomNodeTop(-1000000) when off-screen); references/vscode/src/vs/editor/contrib/codelens/browser/codelensWidget.ts:190-260, :291-296 (same split: CodeLensViewZone reserves px, CodeLensContentWidget renders ABOVE line n+1); references/vscode/src/vs/editor/contrib/peekView/browser/peekView.ts:98-272 (PeekViewWidget adds _fillHead/_fillBody/_doLayoutHead/_doLayoutBody/setTitle/onDidClose on top of ZoneWidget)
mechanism: Monaco never puts widget DOM inside the scrolled line list. A view zone contributes only *whitespace* to the vertical layout; its own DOM node is a stub. The real content is registered as an overlay widget (viewport-fixed, absolutely positioned), and the zone's `onDomNodeTop(top)` callback pushes the scrolled top onto that overlay node each render. Consequences: the widget's DOM is created once and never re-parented, so focus, text selection, an embedded editor's scroll position, IME composition and iframe state all survive scrolling; the widget can be clipped to the editor bounds; and resizing via a sash only changes the whitespace height, not the row list. `ZoneWidget` then layers on the reusable chrome — arrow (a dynamically generated `.arrow-decoration-N` CSS rule positioned via a decoration), frame borders, `_decoratingElementsHeight()` subtracting arrow+frame from the body height, `_getMaximumHeightInLines()` capping at 80% of the viewport, and `revealRange` after showing. `PeekViewWidget` subclasses it into title bar + action bar + body with `_doLayoutHead/_doLayoutBody`.
whyItMatters: Our block surfaces are the right *idea* but mount into recycled virtual rows, so any interactive surface (a diff comment box, an inline chat input, an embedded preview, a peek result list) loses focus and internal state the moment the user scrolls it out and back. That is a hard ceiling on what block surfaces can be used for. Splitting space-reservation from DOM hosting removes the ceiling without changing the public `EditorBlock` API, and gives us the ZoneWidget/PeekView building block for free.
ourEvidence: We have space-reserving zones: `packages/editor/src/editorBlocks.ts:1-82` (`EditorBlock` with top/bottom `EditorBlockHorizontalSurface` and a `mount(container, ctx)` callback, `FixedSize | MinSize | MaxSize | BoundedSize`), resolved in `packages/editor/src/editor/blockSurfaceController.ts:42-115` and turned into `BlockRow` (`packages/editor/src/displayTransforms.ts:110-118`). But `packages/editor/src/virtualization/virtualizedTextViewRows.ts:697-727` mounts the surface *into the recycled row element*: `syncBlockRowMount` keys on `row.blockMountKey === blockRow.id` and otherwise calls `disposeBlockRowMount`, which invokes the mount disposable and then `resetBlockContainerElement` — `element.replaceChildren()` plus stripping every attribute. So scrolling a block surface out of the mounted window tears its DOM down and re-runs `mount` on return. There is no overlay-hosted variant and no ZoneWidget/PeekView abstraction anywhere in the repo (grep for `zoneWidget`/`peek` in `packages/*/src` returns nothing).
implementationSketch: Add a `hosting: 'inline' | 'overlay'` field to `EditorBlockHorizontalSurface`. For `'overlay'`, `blockSurfaceController` mounts the surface once into the content-widget layer from finding #3 (or a sibling `editor-block-overlay` layer) and keeps it alive for the block's lifetime; the virtualized row then renders only an empty spacer of the measured height. `virtualizedTextViewRows.setBlockRowContent` (:667-685) already syncs a height-only container, so the spacer path is nearly free. Wire the per-frame top: the virtualizer already knows each row's `item.start`, so emit an `onTop(scrolledTop)` callback per overlay block from the same place `syncBlockContainerHeight` runs, and set `display:none` plus `onTop(-1e6)` when the block leaves the viewport (Monaco's exact trick, viewZones.ts:392-397). Once that lands, `ZoneWidget` is ~150 lines on top: an abstract class taking an `EditorBlock` with `showArrow`/`showFrame` options, `_fillContainer`, `_doLayout(height,width)`, and a `PeekViewWidget` subclass adding the title/action bar.
verifierEvidence: Verified exactly as claimed. packages/editor/src/virtualization/virtualizedTextViewRows.ts:697-727: `syncBlockRowMount` early-returns only when `row.blockMountKey === blockRow.id`, otherwise `disposeBlockRowMount` runs the mount disposable and calls `resetBlockContainerElement`, which does `element.replaceChildren()` then strips every attribute in a while loop (:721-728). Additional teardown sites at :568, :652, :983, :1613 and `disposeBlockRowMounts` at :260-262. Reference verified: references/vscode/src/vs/editor/contrib/zoneWidget/browser/zoneWidget.ts:64-85 (`_onDomNodeTop`), and diffEditor/utils.ts:257-265 uses the same pattern.
verifierNotes: Highest-value item in this domain for us. Any block surface holding component state (an editable form, a scrolled diff pane, a video, a focused input) loses it on scroll-out. Fix does not require Monaco's full ZoneWidget: keep the whitespace reservation as-is and add an opt-in 'hoisted' mode where the surface DOM lives in a viewport-fixed overlay and the row render pushes `top` onto it, mirroring onDomNodeTop. title: Injected text as a first-class concept: phantom content at a zero-width anchor, with cursor stops and hit-test payload
referenceLocation: references/vscode/src/vs/editor/common/model.ts:316-360 (InjectedTextOptions: content, inlineClassName, inlineClassNameAffectsLetterSpacing, attachedData, cursorStops; InjectedTextCursorStops Both/Right/Left/None); references/vscode/src/vs/editor/contrib/inlayHints/browser/inlayHintsController.ts:536-560 (addInjectedText builds a decoration with showIfCollapsed + collapseOnReplaceEdit + AlwaysGrowsWhenTypingAtEdges and `[item.anchor.direction]: opts`), :561-566 (addInjectedWhitespace injects U+200A with a width-only class), :599-706 (per-part padding/border-radius, maximumLength trimming with '…', fixed-length column alignment), :411-418 (_getInlayHintLabelPart recovers `attachedData instanceof RenderedInlayHintLabelPart` from the decoration under the mouse); references/vscode/src/vs/editor/contrib/colorPicker/browser/colorDetector.ts:203-243 (color swatch = `before: {content: noBreakWhitespace, inlineClassName: dynamicRule}`); references/vscode/src/vs/editor/contrib/inlineProgress/browser/inlineProgress.ts:23-31 + :91-98 (injected nbsp reserves the space, a content widget at EXACT draws the spinner in it)
mechanism: `before`/`after` on a decoration inject text into the *view* only — the model text, offsets and LSP positions are untouched. Crucially the anchor range may be **empty** (`showIfCollapsed: true`), which is what makes inlay hints possible at all: the hint hangs off a point, not a span. `cursorStops` controls whether the caret can land on either side of the injected run, so arrowing through `foo(⟨name:⟩ 1)` skips the phantom text as one unit. `attachedData` is an arbitrary object recoverable from `getInjectedTextDecorations`/the decoration under the mouse, which is how clicking an inlay hint part resolves back to its `InlayHintLabelPart` for go-to-definition — the hit-testing story that any interactive phantom text needs. `inlineClassNameAffectsLetterSpacing` tells the layout engine the class changes advance widths so measurement is redone. The same primitive powers color swatches, ghost text, inline progress placeholders, and whitespace padding (an injected U+200A with a width-only CSS class).
whyItMatters: Inlay hints (parameter names, inferred types) are the single most-requested modern editor feature and we structurally cannot render them today. The same primitive would also give us CSS colour swatches, inline error text at end-of-line, and ghost text for AI completions — all currently impossible without faking them as whole extra rows.
ourEvidence: `packages/editor/src/inlineMap.ts:186-190` — `inlineRangeFromSpec` does `if (endOffset <= startOffset) return null`, so an `InlineReplacementSpec` must cover at least one real character. Our inline layer *substitutes* existing text (markdown `**` → hidden, `- ` → `•`, see `packages/markdown/src/replacements.ts:103-122`), it cannot *insert* phantom text. `InlineReplacement` (`packages/editor/src/displayTransforms.ts:173-180`) carries `{id, startColumn, endColumn, text, kind?, metadata?}` — no `className`, so injected content cannot be styled differently from surrounding code, and no cursor-stop control (only a global `TransformBias` at `inlineMap.ts:131-142`). `InjectedTextRow` (`displayTransforms.ts:97-106`) injects a whole extra *row* before/after a line, not inline content at a column. `metadata` exists on both, which is the `attachedData` idea already half-present.
implementationSketch: Relax `inlineRangeFromSpec` to accept `endOffset === startOffset` when the spec carries an explicit `insert: true` (or a `showIfCollapsed` flag), anchoring both ends at the same offset with opposing biases so typing at the point pushes the hint aside rather than through it. Add `className` and `cursorStops: 'both' | 'left' | 'right' | 'none'` to `InlineReplacementSpec`/`InlineReplacement`, and thread `className` into the segment rendering in `createInlineRow` (`displayTransforms.ts:318-340`) so injected runs get their own span class. `cursorStops` then becomes an override on the `TransformBias` used by `inlineColumnToSourceColumn` for caret motion — our existing `revealInlineMap` machinery must NOT reveal insertion-kind specs, so gate reveal on `kind`. `metadata` already gives us `attachedData`; expose an `inlineReplacementAtPoint(clientX, clientY)` lookup for hit-testing. With that, an inlay-hints controller in `packages/lsp-plugin` is a straightforward LSP `textDocument/inlayHint` consumer emitting specs through the existing display-projection registry.
verifierEvidence: The core gap is real: packages/editor/src/inlineMap.ts:186 `if (endOffset <= startOffset) return null` blocks point-anchored phantom text, so inlay hints are impossible. But two sub-claims are FALSE. (a) 'no className, so injected content cannot be styled differently' — packages/editor/src/virtualization/virtualizedTextViewRows.ts:1536-1566 `updateRowInlineKindClasses` mirrors every replacement's `kind` onto the row element as `editor-inline-<kind>` (guarded by CLASS_SAFE_REPLACEMENT_KIND at :1534), which packages/markdown already relies on for heading styling; covered by packages/editor/test/inlineReplacementPainting.test.ts:61,69. (b) 'hit-test payload missing' — `metadata` flows spec → InlineReplacementRange → InlineReplacement (displayTransforms.ts:173-180) → InlineRowSegment.metadata (:184-190) → EditorVisibleRowSnapshot.metadata (plugins.ts:~152) and EditorGutterRowContext.metadata (plugins.ts:396). title: Replacing a text range with an arbitrary DOM node, and collapsed marks spanning multiple lines
referenceLocation: references/codemirror5/src/model/mark_text.js:166-172 (replacedWith → marker.collapsed = true, marker.widgetNode = eltP('span',[node],'CodeMirror-widget'), cm-ignore-events unless handleMouseEvents, insertLeft), :173-179 (collapsed markers may span line boundaries; partial overlap of two collapsed markers throws), :185-198 (updateLineHeight(line,0) for fully-swallowed lines; clearOnEnter → beforeCursorEnter clears the mark), :205-217 (collapsed ⇒ atomic ⇒ reCheckSelection so the caret cannot land inside), :254-256 (widgetNode cloned per document for shared/linked docs)
mechanism: CodeMirror's `markText` with `replacedWith: domNode` swaps a text span for a real DOM node in the inline flow. The mark is implicitly `collapsed` (the underlying text produces no glyphs) and implicitly `atomic` (`mark_text.js:205-207`), so selection and cursor motion treat it as a single indivisible unit and `reCheckSelection` pushes the caret out if an edit would strand it inside. Because collapsing is a line-*spans* operation rather than a per-line substitution, a collapsed mark may swallow whole intermediate lines: those lines get `updateLineHeight(line, 0)` and the visual line is stitched from the surrounding fragments. `handleMouseEvents: false` stamps `cm-ignore-events` so the editor's own mouse handling ignores the widget's subtree; `insertLeft` controls which side of the mark's position an insertion lands on.
whyItMatters: Our markdown WYSIWYG is explicitly 'a view over the same piece-table buffer'. Text-to-text substitution gets us `**bold**` → bold and `- ` → `•`, but it cannot render an inline image, a rendered LaTeX span, a clickable checkbox, or a colour swatch — all of which need a DOM node, not a string. The multi-line restriction also means a fenced code block or a multi-line link reference can't be collapsed into a single rendered widget.
ourEvidence: `packages/editor/src/inlineMap.ts:207-213` (`normalizeInlineRanges`) filters `.filter(range => range.startPoint.row === range.endPoint.row)` and `.filter(range => !range.text.includes('\n'))` — replacements are strictly single-line, single-row, text-only. `InlineReplacement` (`packages/editor/src/displayTransforms.ts:173-180`) has `text: string` and no node/element field. `InlineRowSegment` (`displayTransforms.ts:184-190`) is purely column arithmetic. On the plus side, `revealInlineMap` (`inlineMap.ts:88-118`) plus `groupId` already give us the atomic/`clearOnEnter` behaviour — the caret entering a hidden span reveals the whole group — so the hard interaction semantics are solved; only the rendering substrate is missing.
implementationSketch: Add an optional `render?: (container: HTMLElement) => void | EditorDisposable` alongside `text` on `InlineReplacementSpec`. In the row painter, a segment whose replacement carries `render` produces an `inline-block` span with `contenteditable=false` that the callback fills, keyed and mount-cached exactly like `syncBlockRowMount` does for block rows (`virtualizedTextViewRows.ts:697-713`) — but note finding #4: cache the mount by replacement id across row recycling or the widget will thrash. Advance-width measurement is the real cost: the segment's display width is no longer `text.length * charWidth`, so `virtualizedTextViewGeometry` needs a measured-width path per rendered replacement (reuse the ResizeObserver plumbing already in `editorBlockSurfaces.ts`). Multi-line collapsing is a separate, larger change to `foldMap`+`inlineMap` interaction and should be deferred; single-line DOM replacement alone unlocks images, checkboxes and swatches.
verifierEvidence: Verified. packages/editor/src/inlineMap.ts:207-213 `normalizeInlineRanges` filters `range.startPoint.row === range.endPoint.row` and `!range.text.includes('\n')`. `InlineReplacement` (displayTransforms.ts:173-180) is `text: string` with no node field; `InlineRowSegment` (:184-190) is pure column arithmetic. title: View zone knobs we lack: ordinal tiebreak, before-first-line, render-in-hidden-areas, margin twin, min scroll width, suppressMouseDown
referenceLocation: references/vscode/src/vs/editor/browser/editorBrowser.ts:36-101 (IViewZone: afterLineNumber with 0 = before first line, afterColumn + afterColumnAffinity, showInHiddenAreas, ordinal, suppressMouseDown, heightInLines vs heightInPx, minWidthInPx, marginDomNode, onDomNodeTop, onComputedHeight), :104-125 (IViewZoneChangeAccessor addZone/removeZone/layoutZone); references/vscode/src/vs/editor/browser/viewParts/viewZones/viewZones.ts:143-146 (_getZoneOrdinal = ordinal ?? afterColumn ?? 10000), :148-195 (_computeWhitespaceProps: validates the position, converts model→view position, and zeroes the height when the anchor line is inside a fold unless showInHiddenAreas), :198-230 (changeViewZones batches through an accessor that is invalidated after the callback), :410-412 (marginDomNode width tracks contentLeft)

All mutations go through a short-lived `IViewZoneChangeAccessor` that is deliberately poisoned (`invalidFunc`) after the callback returns, so nobody can stash it and mutate layout outside a batch.
whyItMatters: Each of these is a bug we will hit: two plugins both adding a top surface to line 40 currently order by provider-array position (non-deterministic across plugin registration order); a block surface on a folded line has undefined behaviour; there is no way to put a banner above line 1; a wide block surface won't extend the scroll width; and a block surface can't paint into the gutter lane beside itself. Adopting the field set now is cheap and prevents API churn later.
ourEvidence: `packages/editor/src/editorBlocks.ts:1-82` covers the core: row/range anchor, `top`/`bottom` surfaces with `FixedSize|MinSize|MaxSize|BoundedSize` (richer than Monaco's heightInPx/heightInLines), `left`/`right` lane surfaces (Monaco has no equivalent — this is ours to keep), and a `mount` callback. title: Preserve the visual anchor when content height changes above the viewport
referenceLocation: references/codemirror5/src/model/line_widget.js:53-57 (adjustScrollWhenAboveVisible: if heightAtLine(line) < scrollTop, addToScrollTop(cm, diff)), :59-76 (addLineWidget computes aboveVisible before updateLineHeight and compensates by the widget height), :36-49 (LineWidget.changed() recomputes height and applies the same compensation for a resize)
mechanism: Whenever a line widget is added, removed or resized, CodeMirror checks whether the widget's line sits *above* the current scrollTop. If so it adds the height delta straight into scrollTop, so the pixels the user is looking at do not move. `LineWidget.clear()` applies the negative delta and `LineWidget.changed()` applies the delta on resize — all three mutation paths are covered, and the compensation happens inside the same operation as the height change, so there is no intermediate frame where the content has jumped.

title: Range-highlight paint order is registration-order dependent, so overlapping decorations can swap z-order after scrolling

mechanism: Monaco makes stacking an explicit, declared property of each decoration and sorts by it deterministically at render time, then merges only same-zIndex peers. Order never depends on when a decoration was created or whether it was momentarily empty.
whyItMatters: We paint range decorations through the CSS Custom Highlight API, where paint order for equal-priority highlights is *registration order in the `CSS.highlights` registry*. Our code never sets `Highlight.priority`, and it deregisters a group whenever it momentarily has zero mounted ranges — then re-registers it later, which moves it to the end of the registry. Concrete repro: with a find-match highlight overlapping the current selection, scroll all matches out of the mounted window (group hits `highlight.size === 0` → `unregisterRangeHighlight`), then scroll back; the group re-registers *after* the selection highlight and now paints on top of it, inverting the colours the user saw a moment ago. The same applies between any two overlapping groups — diagnostics vs occurrences, bracket match vs selection.
ourEvidence: `packages/editor/src/virtualization/virtualizedTextViewHighlights.ts:1306-1315` — `ensureRangeHighlightRegistered` does `view.highlightRegistry.set(group.name, group.highlight)` with no `group.highlight.priority` assignment; grep for `priority` in `packages/editor/src/virtualization/*.ts` returns nothing. `renderRangeHighlight` (:260-279) calls `unregisterRangeHighlight` whenever `group.highlight.size === 0` — i.e. whenever no range of that group is currently mounted — and re-registers on return. implementationSketch: Two-part fix. (1) Add `zIndex?: number` to `EditorRangeDecoration`, default it from the owning projection's `layer`/`priority` in `Editor.composedRangeDecorations` (`Editor.ts:2103-2107`), include it in `rangeDecorationGroupKey` (`rangeDecorations.ts:81-91`), and set `group.highlight.priority = zIndex` in `ensureRangeHighlightRegistered`. That makes paint order declared rather than incidental. (2) Stop deregistering on transient emptiness — in `renderRangeHighlight` (:272-276) keep the group registered with an empty `Highlight` when it has ranges in the model but none currently mounted, and only deregister in `clearRangeHighlight`. Sort groups by zIndex in `groupedRangeDecorations` before assigning indices so group names are stable across frames too. A regression test can assert `CSS.highlights` iteration order/priority is unchanged across a mount-out/mount-in cycle.
verifierEvidence: The defect is REAL but the claimed cause is wrong. Under the CSS Custom Highlight API, equal-priority highlights paint in HighlightRegistry insertion order, and `renderRangeHighlight` (:273-278) unregisters any group whose `highlight.size === 0` — i.e. whenever none of its ranges is currently mounted — then re-registers it at the tail on return. verifierNotes: Cheapest real bug in the list: assign `group.highlight.priority` from the owning projection's layer/priority in `ensureRangeHighlightRegistered`. Note our substrate differs from Monaco's — we do not merge same-zIndex peers into one span, we stack ::highlight() pseudo-elements, so we need priority propagation, not Monaco's sort-and-merge.

title: Refcounted dynamic CSS rule factory: arbitrary per-decoration styling without unbounded stylesheet growth
referenceLocation: references/vscode/src/vs/editor/browser/editorDom.ts:284-345 (DynamicCssRules: _rules keyed by JSON.stringify(properties), createClassNameRef increments a refcount and returns a disposable, a RunOnceScheduler garbage-collects unreferenced rules after 1000ms so hanging rules can be reused), :347-400 (CssProperties whitelist; RefCountedCssRule creates one <style> element per rule and resolves ThemeColor values to `var(--vscode-…)` CSS variables, and targets the shadow root when the editor is in shadow DOM); usage: inlayHintsController.ts:571-706 (a class ref per hint part), colorDetector.ts:200-243 (a class ref per colour swatch)
mechanism: Features that need genuinely dynamic styling (a colour swatch whose background is the literal parsed colour; an inlay hint whose font-size/padding/border-radius derives from options) cannot use static CSS classes. `DynamicCssRules` hashes the property bag, reuses an existing rule for identical properties, hands out `{className, dispose}` and garbage-collects only after a 1s delay — which is the key trick: a re-render that disposes and immediately re-creates the same rule hits the cache instead of churning the stylesheet. `ThemeColor` values become CSS custom-property references rather than literals, so a theme switch needs no rule regeneration at all.
whyItMatters: Our decoration styling is limited to three properties applied through `::highlight()`, which cannot express borders, padding, border-radius, inline-block widths, or `::before` content — everything an inlay hint, colour swatch, or ghost-text run needs. title: Overlay widgets: declarative corner anchoring with stacking, and widget min-width feeding the editor's scroll width

mechanism: Overlay widgets are viewport-fixed rather than document-anchored. whyItMatters: Our find widget, and any future 'N problems' bar, breadcrumb, or read-only banner, each hand-position themselves against the scroll element and none of them know about each other. Port the `stackCoordinates` accumulation verbatim (overlayWidgets.ts:167-213); it is ~40 lines. Feed the aggregated min-width into the virtualizer's content-width computation (`virtualizedTextViewGeometry.ts`) so wide overlays extend the scroll range. title: Find-in-selection scope is recomputed from the live selection, so it is destroyed by the first replace and silently widens to the whole document

Separately, make `normalizedSearchRanges` distinguish 'no scope' (null) from 'empty scope' (a scope that collapsed to nothing must yield zero matches, never the full document). Trace: `replaceOne` (findController.ts:201-205) applies the edit with a collapsed selection; the resulting view update reaches `handleViewUpdate`, which passes the `kind === 'content'` guard (:304 only skips `selection`/`none` changes) and hits :311-312 `if (this.state.inSelection) this.scopes = nonEmptySelectionRanges(...)`; `nonEmptySelectionRanges` (:521-527) filters collapsed selections, so `this.scopes` becomes `[]`; `findAll` passes `[]` to `normalizedSearchRanges`, which at search.ts:107 treats `ranges.length === 0` identically to `null` and returns `[{start: 0, end: text.length}]`. `toggleFindInSelection` (:271-286) stores raw offsets with no whole-line normalization. title: Seeding the search string from the selection does not escape regex metacharacters when regex mode is on

title: Replace-pattern edge cases: out-of-range $nn should degrade digit-by-digit, and a backslash should swallow the next character
referenceLocation: vscode/src/vs/editor/contrib/find/browser/replacePattern.ts:108-127 (_substitute), :238-287 (the backslash branch consumes the next char unconditionally, with no default case), :215-229 (the documented grammar); vscode/src/vs/editor/contrib/find/test/browser/replacePattern.test.ts
mechanism: Monaco's `_substitute` for an index beyond the capture count peels digits off the right: `while (matchIndex > 0) { if (matchIndex < matches.length) return (matches[matchIndex] || '') + remainder; remainder = String(matchIndex % 10) + remainder; matchIndex = Math.floor(matchIndex / 10); }`. So with one capture group, `$12` renders as `<group 1>` followed by a literal `2` — matching what users expect from sed/JS semantics — and only falls back to a literal `$…` when even the first digit is out of range. Separately, the parser's backslash branch does `i++` before the switch and has *no* default case, so an unrecognized escape like `\$` consumes both characters: `\$1` stays the literal three characters and is never treated as a capture reference.
whyItMatters: Both are small, but both are the kind of thing a user hits once and then stops trusting regex replace. `$12` silently emitting the literal text `$12` into their code, or `\$1` unexpectedly expanding to a capture, are the sort of quiet wrong-output bugs that are hard to notice in a bulk replace.

Port Monaco's replacePattern.test.ts cases wholesale — the file is 254 lines and covers exactly these corners.

Out-of-range: our replacePattern.ts:185-190 `substituteMatch` returns the literal `` `$${index}` `` with no peeling; Monaco's references/vscode/src/vs/editor/contrib/find/browser/replacePattern.ts:104-121 `_substitute` peels digits off the right (`remainder = String(matchIndex % 10) + remainder`). On each cursor/content change `_onNewContext` classifies the delta: cursor moved left → retrigger if still on a word, else cancel; leading whitespace changed → cancel; a *new* word started → retrigger but pass the entire current item map as `providerItemsToReuse`; cursor moved right and at least one provider marked its list `incomplete` → build a `providerFilter` of *only* the incomplete providers and a `providerItemsToReuse` of all the complete ones, and retrigger with `CompletionTriggerKind.TriggerForIncompleteCompletions`; otherwise → no request at all, just update `completionModel.lineContext` and re-filter locally. Trigger characters get the same treatment (:280-296): typing `.` re-asks only the providers that declare `.` and keeps everyone else's items. There is also a 'freeze' behaviour (:800-822): when the user *manually* invoked suggest and filtering has emptied the list, the old lineContext is restored and the widget stays up rather than vanishing mid-word.
whyItMatters: This is the difference between a suggest widget that feels continuous and one that flickers. It also fixes a real correctness hole: `CompletionList.isIncomplete` from a server means 'ask me again as the user types', and a client that ignores it shows a stale, wrongly-filtered list for large member sets (TS auto-import completions are always incomplete).

On a `content` update, compute the new prefix via `completionPrefix()`; if the caret is still inside the same word and the prefix *extends* the request prefix, re-filter locally (no request) unless `isIncomplete`, in which case re-request and replace. Cancel only on the conditions Monaco cancels on: line changed, leading-whitespace changed, caret left the word. Stop hiding on `selection` updates that are the consequence of typing. Since we currently have a single provider, `providerItemsToReuse` collapses to 'keep or replace the whole list' until the registry from finding #1 lands, at which point the per-provider maps become necessary.

[]` and never reads `isIncomplete`; grep for `isIncomplete` across packages/ hits only the *producing* side — packages/typescript-lsp/src/typescriptLsp.worker.ts:592, :634 (`isIncomplete: info.isIncomplete === true`) and its tests — so our own TS server already reports the flag and the client throws it away. packages/lsp-plugin/src/completionController.ts:68-90 `update()` calls `this.hide()` on kind `document`/`clear`/`selection`/`viewport`/`layout` and on any `content` change where `completionTriggerFromChange` returns null; completion.ts:157-172 that trigger only fires for a single-character edit that is an identifier char or a trigger char, so backspace, paste, and multi-char IME commits all close the widget. title: Snippet engine: placeholder mirrors, transforms with regex + case-shorthands, choices, and indentation normalization

mechanism: Snippets parse into a marker tree, not a string+ranges pair. Each stop's decoration options are swapped on every `move()`: the active stop uses grow-on-edge stickiness while inactive ones use never-grow, which is precisely what makes typing at a placeholder boundary do the right thing. Transforms (`${1/(.*)/${1:capitalize}/}`) run when the caret *leaves* the stop (:102-125), re-indenting any newlines the transform introduced. `adjustWhitespace` (:427) rewrites the template's Text markers before insertion so a multi-line snippet lands at the caller's indentation and in the caller's tab style. Nested placeholders are real (`enclosingPlaceholders`), and `_hasPlaceholderBeenCollapsed` (:189-210) skips a stop the user has emptied.
whyItMatters: Everything past `${1:name}` in our parser is silently lossy, and mirrors are the single most-noticed snippet feature (rename a `$1` and every copy follows). LSP servers routinely ship snippets with transforms and choices; TypeScript's own `Method Signature` completions use nested placeholders.

title: Re-diffing formatter output into minimal edits before applying it
referenceLocation: vscode/src/vs/editor/common/services/editorWebWorker.ts:218-298 ($computeMoreMinimalEdits); called from vscode/src/vs/editor/contrib/format/browser/format.ts:245-247 (range formatting) and the document-formatting path around :290-330
mechanism: Formatter results are never applied as given. The worker sorts the edits, merges adjacent ones (:238-248), drops no-ops (`original === text`, :264-267), normalizes EOLs to the model's, and then — for each remaining edit under a `_diffLimit` size cap — runs a character-level `stringDiff` between the *current* text in the range and the replacement, emitting one small edit per change region mapped back through `model.offsetAt/positionAt` (:276-290). A single whole-document replacement from `prettier`/`tsserver` therefore becomes a handful of tiny edits. Each produced edit is checked once more against the model before being kept (:287).
whyItMatters: Directly determines whether formatting destroys editor state. A whole-buffer replace invalidates every anchor, decoration, fold, and selection, blows out the undo stack as one giant entry, and makes the whole viewport repaint. With minimal edits, the caret stays put, folds survive, and a no-op format is genuinely a no-op. It matters more for us than for Monaco because our anchors and fold map are offset-tracked.
ourEvidence: packages/lsp-plugin/src/formatting.ts:13-38 — `formattingEdits()` converts LSP edits, sorts, drops overlaps, reverses, and returns them raw; there is no diffing step. `formattingChangesText` (:42-44) only decides whether *anything* changed, it does not minimize. We already have the diff primitive: packages/editor/src/pieceTable/diff.ts.
implementationSketch: Add a `minimizeFormattingEdits(text, edits)` step inside `packages/lsp-plugin/src/formatting.ts`, between the overlap filter and the reverse: for each edit whose `to - from` and `text.length` are both under a cap (say 100k), run the existing `packages/editor/src/pieceTable/diff.ts` routine over `text.slice(from, to)` vs `edit.text`, and expand into per-change-region edits offset by `from`; skip edits whose diff is empty. Merge adjacent edits first, exactly as the reference does, so a formatter that emits per-line edits does not defeat the diff. Existing tests in packages/lsp-plugin should be extended with a 'whole-document replace that changes one line' case asserting a single small edit comes out.
verifierEvidence: Confirmed. packages/lsp-plugin/src/formatting.ts:13-38 `formattingEdits` converts LSP positions to offsets, sorts ascending by `from` (longest first on ties), drops any edit starting before `keptThrough`, and reverses — no minimization, no adjacent-edit merge, no no-op drop, no EOL normalization. :42-44 `formattingChangesText` is a boolean over the whole set. Crucially, the cost is documented in our own code: packages/lsp-plugin/src/plugin.ts:586-591 comments 'The caret is pinned to its offset rather than tracked through the edits: formatting moves text wholesale' and then :592-596 `applyFormattingEdits` sets `selection: { anchor: head, head }` from the pre-format offset. Primitives available: packages/editor/src/pieceTable/diff.ts:11 `diffPieceTableSnapshots` (prefix/suffix only — produces ONE edit, not a change list, so it is not sufficient alone), and packages/diff/src/inline.ts:1 already imports `diffWordsWithSpace` from the npm `diff` package, so a real change-list diff is already a monorepo dependency. Minimizing formatter output is what makes the caret, the selection, folds, diagnostics anchors and inline-replacement anchors survive a format instead of being reset; with a whole-document edit every anchor in packages/editor/src/pieceTable/anchors.ts dies at once. Correction to the claim's evidence: packages/editor/src/pieceTable/diff.ts is NOT the right primitive (it returns a single prefix/suffix edit); use the `diff` package already vendored for packages/diff, and apply Monaco's size cap so a 5 MB minified file does not run a quadratic diff. title: Completion insert-vs-replace ranges: we silently drop the replace range
referenceLocation: vscode/src/vs/editor/contrib/suggest/browser/suggest.ts:100-120 (CompletionItem normalizes range into editStart/editInsertEnd/editReplaceEnd and validates single-line-ness); suggestController.ts:573-589 (getOverwriteInfo: picks insert or replace end per `suggest.insertMode`, adds `columnDelta` for characters typed since the request went out, and `suffixDelta` from the OvertypingCapturer); :209 (ctxHasInsertAndReplace) and :684 (AlternativeOverwriteConfig — shift+Enter inverts the mode for one acceptance); suggestOvertypingCapturer.ts:10-74
mechanism: An LSP/Monaco completion carries two end positions: `insert` (replace only up to the caret) and `replace` (replace the whole word the caret sits in). Monaco keeps both, validates that neither spans lines and that they share a start column, and at acceptance computes `overwriteBefore = caretColumn - editStart.column` and `overwriteAfter = (replace ? editReplaceEnd : editInsertEnd).column - caretColumn`, then *adds* `columnDelta` — the number of characters typed between the request and the acceptance — so a completion accepted after further typing still overwrites the right span. `suffixDelta` restores text the user overtyped over a selection. Shift+Enter flips insert/replace for a single acceptance.
whyItMatters: With `foo|Bar` in the buffer and accepting `foobaz`, insert mode gives `foobazBar` and replace mode gives `foobaz`. We always take the insert range, so accepting a completion in the middle of an existing identifier leaves the tail behind — a visible, frequently-hit bug. The `columnDelta` correction matters too: our 80 ms debounce guarantees the user has often typed more since the request.
ourEvidence: packages/lsp-plugin/src/completion.ts:388-393 — `completionTextEdit()` for an `InsertReplaceEdit` returns `{ range: textEdit.insert, newText }`, discarding `.replace` unconditionally. `completionApplication` (:174-194) uses the offset captured at request time (`session.offset` in completionController.ts:213, :266) with no delta for characters typed since. No validation that the edit range is single-line. No insert/replace toggle key.
implementationSketch: Change `completionTextEdit` to return both ends, and add an `insertMode: 'insert' | 'replace'` option (default 'replace', which is what most users expect and what TypeScript assumes) threaded through `CompletionControllerOptions`. In `completionApplication`, compute the replacement span from the chosen end and add `currentOffset - session.offset` to it, validating the LSP range is on one line and rejecting the item otherwise (Monaco's `isInvalid`). Bind Shift+Enter in `handleCompletionKeyDown` (completionController.ts:293-330) to accept with the mode inverted.
verifierEvidence: Confirmed, but the blast radius is smaller than stated. packages/lsp-plugin/src/completion.ts:388-393 `completionTextEdit` — for an `InsertReplaceEdit` it returns `{ range: textEdit.insert, newText }`, dropping `.replace`. However :423-433 `defaultCompletionReplacementRange` — the path taken when the item has NO textEdit — already walks identifier characters both backwards AND forwards from the offset, i.e. it already implements *replace* semantics for the common case. So the defect is confined to servers that send InsertReplaceEdit (our own tsserver bridge at packages/typescript-lsp/src/typescriptLsp.worker.ts:634-652 does not appear to). Staleness confirmed: completionController.ts:213 stores `this.completionSession = { active, offset }` at show time and :266 `completionApplication(session.active.fullText, session.offset, item)` re-uses it at accept time with no adjustment for characters typed in between. No single-line validation of the edit range, and no insert/replace toggle key (completionController.ts:293-330 handles only ArrowUp/Down, PageUp/Down, Escape, Enter, Tab).
verifierNotes: Keep, but re-prioritise inside the claim. The InsertReplaceEdit drop is a two-line fix and low impact given our default path already replaces the whole word. The *stale offset* is the real bug and is worth calling out separately: accept the completion after typing two more characters and the edit is computed against an offset that no longer matches the buffer. Monaco's `overwriteBefore = caretColumn - editStart.column` / `overwriteAfter` reformulation is the fix worth copying — it re-derives the range from the *current* caret rather than the request-time offset, which makes the whole class of races go away. The user-facing insert/replace toggle key is polish; skip it.

title: Format-on-type, gated by provider trigger characters and cancelled by any edit before the caret
referenceLocation: vscode/src/vs/editor/contrib/format/browser/formatActions.ts:31-150 (FormatOnType: _update builds a CharacterSet from `support.autoFormatTriggerCharacters` at :80-93; _trigger at :97 bails on multi-cursor or non-empty selection, then installs an onDidChangeModelContent guard at :111-129 that cancels the in-flight request if any change lands at or before the caret's line, or on a model flush), :155-230 (FormatOnPaste, triggered from editor.onDidPaste with the pasted range)
mechanism: Format-on-type is not 'format the line after every keystroke'. The provider declares which characters may trigger it (`}`, `;`, newline for TS), the editor builds a `CharacterSet` once per model/option change, and only those characters fire a `textDocument/onTypeFormatting` request. Because the request is async and the user keeps typing, a listener watches for content changes while it is in flight and cancels if a change occurred at or before the caret's line — otherwise the returned edits, computed for an older document, would corrupt text the user has since typed. Format-on-paste is the same machinery keyed on the paste range instead of a character.
whyItMatters: Auto-indenting a closing brace, re-spacing a statement on `;`, and reformatting pasted code are the three highest-frequency formatting interactions; document-level formatting is the rare one. The cancellation guard is the non-obvious part and is exactly the class of bug that produces duplicated or scrambled text.
ourEvidence: Only `textDocument/formatting` is requested anywhere in packages/ (grep over packages/lsp-plugin/src, packages/lsp/src, packages/typescript-lsp/src yields no `onTypeFormatting` and no `rangeFormatting`). packages/lsp-plugin/src/formatting.ts has no trigger-character or paste path. `documentOnTypeFormattingProvider` capability is not advertised in packages/lsp/src/capabilities.ts.
implementationSketch: Add an `OnTypeFormattingController` in packages/lsp-plugin/src modelled on `documentHighlightController.ts`: read `serverCapabilities.documentOnTypeFormattingProvider.{firstTriggerCharacter, moreTriggerCharacter}` (already reachable via `this.client.serverCapabilities`), build a Set once per connection, and hook the same `update(snapshot, kind, change)` path CompletionController uses (`kind === 'content'` with a single-character edit) to fire the request. Reuse `latestAsyncRequest.ts` for cancellation, plus an explicit guard: capture the document version/snapshot identity at request time and drop the result if any edit landed at or before the request offset — our `DocumentSessionChange` carries edit offsets so this is a cheap comparison. Route the result through the same `formattingEdits()` (with the minimization from finding #5). Paste is a second trigger on the same controller.
verifierEvidence: Confirmed. Grepping `'textDocument/` across packages/lsp-plugin/src returns exactly: completion, definition, implementation, typeDefinition, references, documentHighlight, hover, signatureHelp, rename, formatting, publishDiagnostics (plugin.ts:560 is the only formatting request). packages/typescript-lsp/src/typescriptLsp.worker.ts:143-157 handles hover/completion/definition/references/implementation/typeDefinition/didOpen/didChange/didClose — no onTypeFormatting, no rangeFormatting. packages/lsp/src/capabilities.ts:11-49 advertises only synchronization, completion and signatureHelp; `documentOnTypeFormattingProvider` is absent. Separately confirmed we have no local substitute: packages/editor/src/editor/indentation.ts exports only `lineBreakIndent` and `leadingWhitespace`, and packages/editor/src/editor/indentation.test.ts:41-64 covers 'indents one level deeper after an opener' and 'pushes a closer onto its own line' — i.e. indent-on-Enter only. title: Semantic tokens: delta protocol with in-place Uint32Array splicing
referenceLocation: vscode/src/vs/editor/contrib/semanticTokens/browser/documentSemanticTokens.ts:245 (lastResultId passed to the provider), :296-400 (_setDocumentSemanticTokens: SemanticTokensEdits branch at :325-380, empty-edits fast path at :331-337, backwards splice loop at :348-372, _copy at :288-295), plus `releaseDocumentSemanticTokens(resultId)` (:311, :421) and the pending-changes reschedule (:296-305); provider interface at vscode/src/vs/editor/common/languages.ts:2488-2499
mechanism: The provider is asked `provideDocumentSemanticTokens(model, lastResultId, token)` and may answer either a full `SemanticTokens` (flat Uint32Array of 5-tuples: deltaLine, deltaStartChar, length, tokenType, tokenModifiers) or a `SemanticTokensEdits` — a list of `{ start, deleteCount, data }` splices *against the previous array*. Invalid edit starts are detected and the whole result discarded rather than producing garbage (:350-354). `releaseDocumentSemanticTokens(resultId)` tells the provider it may drop its cached previous result. Content changes that arrive while a request is in flight are accumulated and force a reschedule rather than being applied to stale tokens (:296-305).
whyItMatters: Semantic tokens are the layer that distinguishes a type from a variable from a parameter — the thing tree-sitter alone cannot do for TypeScript. Add a `SemanticTokensController` in packages/lsp-plugin that advertises `textDocument.semanticTokens` with `full: { delta: true }` in capabilities.ts, holds `{ resultId, data: Uint32Array }`, and ports the backwards splice loop verbatim. verifierEvidence: Confirmed absent: grep for `semanticToken|SemanticToken` across packages/ (all .ts) returns zero hits, and packages/lsp/src/capabilities.ts:11-49 does not advertise `textDocument.semanticTokens`. Highlighting is tree-sitter (packages/tree-sitter/*, packages/editor/src/syntax/session.ts) plus shiki (packages/editor/src/shiki/). title: Inline completions / ghost text: deriving renderable inline parts from an arbitrary text edit
referenceLocation: vscode/src/vs/editor/contrib/inlineCompletions/browser/model/computeGhostText.ts:19-118 (computeGhostText), :36-62 (indentation-touching special case), :120-152 (cachingDiff with a smartness retry), :162-215 (smartDiff: bracket-aware LCS by remapping '(' and ')' to synthetic char codes so `if ()` aligns against `if (f() = 1)` correctly); model/ghostText.ts:16-160 (GhostText/GhostTextPart/GhostTextReplacement); model/inlineCompletionIsVisible.ts:12-30
mechanism: An inline suggestion arrives as a plain `TextReplacement` (range + text), which may replace text, not just append. `computeGhostText` first strips the common prefix, rejects multi-line edits whose first lines are not a pure prefix, then handles the indentation case explicitly (a suggestion that starts inside the line's leading whitespace is re-based so ghost text never re-renders existing indentation). title: Debounces with no maximum wait starve syntax refresh under continuous typing
referenceLocation: references/codemirror5/src/util/misc.js:31-55 (class Delayed — `set(ms,f)` only re-arms when `!this.id || time < this.time`), used by references/codemirror5/src/display/highlight_worker.js:10-13 (startWorker) and re-armed mid-slice at :44-47; references/vscode/src/vs/base/common/async.ts:499-522 (ThrottledDelayer = Delayer ∘ Throttler), :421-486 (Delayer), :267-345 (Event.debounce with `leading` and `flushOnListenerRemove`)

A repeated `set(100, …)` therefore fires ~100ms after the *first* request, not 100ms after the last — the deadline can only be pulled in, never pushed out. Monaco expresses the same guarantee compositionally: `ThrottledDelayer` runs the delayer's trailing edge through a `Throttler`, so a new request arriving while a run is in flight is queued rather than cancelling it, and `Event.debounce` takes a `leading` flag so the first event in a burst always gets through.

Our syntax refresh debounce is 150ms with no ceiling, so during a continuous typing run the editor never re-tokenizes at all — highlighting stays frozen on stale token positions until the user pauses, and the longer the run the worse the visible drift. The same applies to feature contributions (LSP diagnostics, occurrence highlights) on the same key.

whyItMatters: We already have the *disposable* half of this contract everywhere; what's missing is a producer primitive. Concretely: today one throwing `onChange` handler or one throwing view contribution can abort the rest of the notification pass mid-edit; there is no way to hand a consumer a debounced or throttled view of an editor event without them writing their own timer; and a plugin that leaks subscriptions across mount/unmount is invisible until memory grows.
ourEvidence: packages/editor/src/plugins.ts:27-29 defines `EditorDisposable {dispose(): void}` and it is used consistently as the *subscription* return type (:106, :417, :447-453), but there is no `Emitter`/`Event<T>` producer type anywhere — grep for `class .*Emitter` under packages/*/src returns nothing. Producers are ad-hoc optional callbacks: `options.onChange` invoked bare at Editor.ts:2515 and :2522, `sessionOptions.onChange?.(finalChange)` at Editor.ts:2412, `provider.onDidChangeBlocks?.(…)` at plugins.ts:1207, `onDidChangeInjectedTextRows?.(…)` at :1255, `EditorTextBufferChangeListener` at documentSession.ts:110, `ConflictListener` at mergeConflictPlugin.ts:56. Error handling is per-site and inconsistent — plugins.ts:1033-1038 wraps a registration notification and rolls back on throw, but the change-notification path (Editor.ts:2412-2419) has no try/catch around individual consumers. No debounce/throttle/accumulate operators exist over these callbacks; each consumer that wants one reaches for `EditorWorkScheduler` directly.
implementationSketch: Add `packages/editor/src/editor/emitter.ts`: `type EditorEvent<T> = (listener: (e: T) => void, disposables?: EditorDisposable[]) => EditorDisposable` and `class EditorEmitter<T> { readonly event: EditorEvent<T>; fire(e: T): void; dispose(): void }`. Port three pieces from event.ts and skip the rest: per-listener try/catch routed to an injectable `onListenerError` (:1376-1395), the index-cursor delivery queue for re-entrancy (:1441-1470 — the array-snapshot-plus-index shape, not the shared cross-emitter queue), and `onWillAddFirstListener`/`onDidRemoveLastListener` hooks. Add `EditorEvent.debounce/throttle/once/map` as free functions over the type, implemented on top of our existing `EditorWorkScheduler` rather than raw timers so debounced events inherit priority, cancellation, and the `maxDelayMs` fix from finding 4. Migrate incrementally: `Editor.onChange` and the plugin-host `onDidChange*` hooks first (Editor.ts:2513-2523, plugins.ts:1207/1255), keeping the existing option-callback signatures as thin adapters. In test builds only, wire a listener-count threshold that logs the dominant registration stack (event.ts:1264-1277), which would catch plugin subscription leaks across the mount/unmount cycles in pluginLifecycle.test.ts.

The sharpest concrete defect, which the claim states abstractly, is at documentSession.ts:645: `for (const listener of this.listeners) listener(event)` — no try/catch. title: DisposableStore and a pluggable disposable tracker for leak detection
referenceLocation: references/vscode/src/vs/base/common/lifecycle.ts:229-233 (setDisposableTracker), :85-180 (DisposableTracker — records a Stacktrace per disposable, computeLeakingDisposables, removePrefix noise-trimming of the captured frames), :49-83 (GCBasedDisposableTracker using FinalizationRegistry), :271-284 (trackDisposable/markAsDisposed/setParentOfDisposable), :327-360 (dispose() overloads over single/array/iterable), :380-400 (Disposable base class registering itself with the tracker)
mechanism: `IDisposable` is a one-method interface, exactly like ours, but every construction and disposal routes through two global hooks — `trackDisposable(x)` and `markAsDisposed(x)` — that are no-ops unless a tracker is installed. `DisposableStore.add` also calls `setParentOfDisposable(child, this)`, so the tracker learns the ownership tree, not just a flat set. In tests a tracker is installed that captures a stack per live disposable; `computeLeakingDisposables` walks the graph and reports the ones that were constructed, parented, and never disposed, with the *construction* stack attached and boilerplate frames stripped (:178). `GCBasedDisposableTracker` (:49-83) is the zero-overhead production variant: it registers each disposable with a `FinalizationRegistry` and reports only those collected without ever having been disposed. The ergonomic layer on top — `toDisposable(fn)`, `MutableDisposable` (swap-and-dispose-previous in one assignment), `DisposableMap`, and the `dispose()` overloads that accept a single value, an array, or any iterable — is what makes the pattern cheap enough that people actually use it consistently.
whyItMatters: We have a large plugin surface where every contribution point hands back an `EditorDisposable`, and correctness depends on every host and every plugin disposing every one on unmount. Right now that is enforced only by hand-maintained arrays and code review; a plugin that forgets one leaves a listener, a decoration, or a scheduler entry alive across editor remounts with no test that can catch it.
ourEvidence: packages/editor/src/plugins.ts:27-29 `EditorDisposable`, with `disposeAll(registrations)` and manual arrays repeated at :791, :796, :855, :873, :1036, :1062, :1088, :1112, :1138, :1164, :1300 and a `disposeAll(result)` aggregator at :1311 — the same store-shaped logic re-implemented per contribution kind. `trackLifecycleRegistration` (plugins.ts, used at :1029 and :1055) and `createEditorLifecycleSummary` (Editor.ts:263) show we already want lifecycle visibility, but there is no construction-site attribution and nothing that can answer 'which disposables from this mount are still alive'. There is no `MutableDisposable` equivalent — swap-and-dispose is hand-written, e.g. plugins.ts:1226 and :1274 (`this.…InvalidationDisposables.get(provider)?.dispose()` before re-registering). packages/editor/src/editor/pluginLifecycle.test.ts exists, so there is already a place for the assertion to live.
implementationSketch: Add `packages/editor/src/editor/disposables.ts` with `EditorDisposableStore` (add/clear/dispose, disposes immediately if the store is already disposed — lifecycle.ts:410-460), `toEditorDisposable(fn)`, and `MutableEditorDisposable`. Route creation and disposal through two module-level hooks `trackDisposable`/`markAsDisposed` with a `setEditorDisposableTracker(tracker | null)` setter, defaulting to null so production cost is zero (lifecycle.ts:229-284). Replace the eleven ad-hoc arrays in plugins.ts with stores and the two manual swap sites (:1226, :1274) with `MutableEditorDisposable`. Then in packages/editor/test add a helper that installs a stack-capturing tracker around a mount/unmount cycle and asserts nothing survives — wire it into pluginLifecycle.test.ts first, then make it a shared fixture so every plugin package (find, minimap, gutters, diff, lsp-plugin) gets the same assertion for free.
verifierEvidence:
Status is right, but the claim's central assertion — 'there is no construction-site attribution and nothing that can answer which disposables from this mount are still alive' — is largely refuted. /Users/shaul/Desktop/D/Editor/packages/editor/src/plugins.ts:556 declares `lifecycleRegistrationStack: EditorDisposable[][]`; installPlugin (:843-861) and activatePlugin (:864-879) each push a fresh array, run the plugin body inside try/finally, and pop; every one of the 13 `register*` methods routes its disposable through `trackLifecycleRegistration` (:1279-1284) which pushes onto `lifecycleRegistrationStack.at(-1)` (:1286-1288). So each registration is AUTOMATICALLY attributed to the owning plugin lifecycle with no `_register(...)` call at the site — implicit ownership, which is stronger than VS Code's explicit DisposableStore.add. `lifecycleDisposableFromResult` (:1291-1300) returns a `disposableOnce` (idempotent, :1319-1329) that disposes the plugin's own result then `disposeAll(registrations)`, and disposeAll (:1315-1317) uses `.toReversed()` — reverse-order teardown, same as DisposableStore. Failure rollback exists too (:855, :873 dispose the partial set on a throwing install/activate). The `disposeAll` + manual-array sites the claim lists at :791/:796/:1036/:1062/... are those same registration arrays, not 11 independent re-implementations.

What IS genuinely missing: a global trackDisposable/markAsDisposed hook, construction-site stack capture, and a MutableDisposable (swap-and-dispose is hand-written at plugins.ts:1226 and :1274).
verifierNotes: Keep — but for a hole I found while refuting it, not for the tracker. plugins.ts:1279-1284 reads `if (registrations) registrations.push(disposable)` and SILENTLY DROPS the disposable when `currentLifecycleRegistrations()` returns null (:1286-1288). That is null for every registration made outside the synchronous install/activate body — i.e. anything a plugin registers from an async continuation, a timer, or an event handler after activation. Those registrations are never auto-disposed on unmount and never appear in the lifecycle summary (Editor.ts:263 createEditorLifecycleSummary / :2665). That is a real leak class in a plugin system where async registration is normal (LSP capabilities arriving after initialize, for instance), and it is invisible today. Minimal fix: have the plugin context carry its own owning store so late registrations attribute to the plugin rather than to nothing, and make the null branch loud (log or throw in dev) instead of silent. Add MutableDisposable while there — it is ~10 lines and deletes the hand-written swap at plugins.ts:1226/:1274. SKIP the global tracker + stack capture: with implicit per-lifecycle attribution already in place, the leak surface it would find is almost entirely the null branch above, which is cheaper to close directly. Assertion belongs in the existing packages/editor/src/editor/pluginLifecycle.test.ts.
